question: Among schools with a school-level SAT excellence rate above 0.3, what is the highest ages-5-17 free-meal eligibility rate?
evidence: SAT excellence rate is the share of test takers scoring at least 1500.
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(1.0 * f."Free Meal Count (Ages 5-17)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)", 0)) FROM frpm AS f JOIN satscores AS s ON s.cds = f.cdscode WHERE s.rtype = 'S' AND s.numtsttakr > 0 AND f."Enrollment (Ages 5-17)" > 0 AND 1.0 * s.numge1500 / NULLIF(s.numtsttakr, 0) > 0.3

question: I'm profiling the High Tech High charter network in San Diego. For charter number 756, what is the average number of SAT test takers per school across all of its schools with a San Diego mailing city? Count every school regardless of operational status, and treat a school with no SAT record as having zero test takers. Round the average to two decimals.
evidence: Charter number 756 is the state-issued charter number.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(COALESCE(sc.numtsttakr, 0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_sat_test_takers_per_school FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS sc ON sc.cds = s.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (s.charternum) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.charternum) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 756 AND s.mailcity = 'San Diego'

question: Which set contains the Aven Mindcensor printing that uses the newest card frame? I want the set's name and its release date. Count every printing, including promotional and online-only ones. If several printings share the newest frame, use the most recently released one; if the release dates tie too, list each such set once. Please give me the set name, not its code.
evidence: Frame version: the frame style used for a printing; frame styles are identified by the year that style was introduced.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT s.name AS setname, s.releasedate FROM cards AS c JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE c.name = 'Aven Mindcensor' AND CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE name = 'Aven Mindcensor') AND s.releasedate = (SELECT MAX(s2.releasedate) FROM cards AS c2 JOIN sets AS s2 ON s2.code = c2.setcode WHERE c2.name = 'Aven Mindcensor' AND CASE WHEN (c2.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c2.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE name = 'Aven Mindcensor'))

question: I'm auditing which recent products were never localized for Spanish-speaking markets. Can you find every set released in calendar year 2020 that has no Spanish name? For each of those, I just need the set code and the set's release date.
evidence: By "Spanish name" I mean the Spanish-language version of a set's name.
gold_sql: SELECT s.code, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s WHERE s.releasedate BETWEEN '2020-01-01' AND '2020-12-31' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code AND t.language = 'Spanish' AND NOT t.translation IS NULL) ORDER BY s.releasedate NULLS FIRST, s.code NULLS FIRST

question: I'm cataloguing special-release printings illustrated by Rob Alexander. What is the total converted mana cost across all cards illustrated by Rob Alexander whose original release falls in 2013? Please give me just that total as a single number. By 'released in 2013' I mean the calendar year from 1 January through 31 December 2013, and a card's original release is the original release date recorded on the card itself—cards with no original release date recorded are out of scope. Each card printing counts separately in the total.
evidence: Converted mana cost: the total numeric mana value of a card, e.g. a card costing {4}{W}{W} has a converted mana cost of 6.
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(convertedmanacost) AS total_converted_mana_cost FROM cards WHERE artist = 'Rob Alexander' AND SUBSTRING(CAST(originalreleasedate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2013'

question: I'm assembling a Japanese-language boros deck and want to check which cards need careful rules review. For every card that has a boros watermark and a Japanese printing, please give me: the Japanese card name, the English card type, and the total number of official rulings recorded for that card. A card is identified by its Japanese name together with its English card type - printings that share both count as one card, and if either differs they should be listed as separate cards. The ruling total should add up all ruling entries across every printing of that card, and if a card has no rulings, list it with a total of 0.
evidence: Boros watermark means the watermark is marked 'boros' on the card; a Japanese printing is the foreign data entry in Japanese; rulings are the official rules clarifications recorded for a card.
gold_sql: SELECT f.name AS japanese_card_name, c.type AS card_type, SUM((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM rulings AS r WHERE r.uuid = c.uuid)) AS ruling_count FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON c.uuid = f.uuid WHERE c.watermark = 'boros' AND f.language = 'Japanese' GROUP BY f.name, c.type ORDER BY f.name COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST, c.type COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a localization coverage report. Among the languages into which the card sets themselves were translated (i.e., have a set translation), which language has the fewest printings whose flavor text was translated into that language? Please give me the language name and the number of such printings. If several languages tie for the fewest, list all of them, ordered alphabetically by language name.
evidence: Set translation: a card set's official release in another language.
gold_sql: WITH set_langs AS (SELECT DISTINCT language FROM set_translations), counts AS (SELECT fd.language, COUNT(*) AS printings FROM foreign_data AS fd WHERE fd.language IN (SELECT language FROM set_langs) AND NOT fd.flavortext IS NULL AND fd.flavortext <> '' GROUP BY fd.language) SELECT language, printings FROM counts WHERE printings = (SELECT MIN(printings) FROM counts) ORDER BY language ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm building a French-language cube and want some big finishers for it. How many different creature cards with power 10 or greater have at least one printing in a set whose name has a French translation? Please return just that single number. Note: a set qualifies based on its name having a French translation, no matter when it was released or what type of set it is, and a card counts if any of its printings comes from such a set.
evidence: French translation: the set's name as given in French.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS total_creature_cards FROM cards WHERE CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 10 AND CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' AND setcode IN (SELECT setcode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'French' AND NOT translation IS NULL)

question: Following up on the SAT participation review: among the currently operating high schools in the district with NCES identification number 0613360 that had no SAT test takers, which one begins serving students at the earliest grade? Please give me each such school's name and grade span served. Note that a high school must actually enroll students through grade 12-offering grade 12 without enrollment doesn't count. A school with no SAT record counts as having zero SAT test takers and should be included; only exclude schools with a positive number of SAT test takers. Compare starting grades as school grades-preschool comes before kindergarten, which comes before grade 1-and use the lowest grade the school actually serves, not just what it offers. If several schools tie at the earliest grade, list them all alphabetically by school name.
evidence: NCES identification number 0613360 is the school district identification number assigned by the National Center for Education Statistics.
gold_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.gsserved AS grade_span_served, CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1) = 'P' THEN -1 WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1) = 'K' THEN 0 ELSE CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION('-' IN s.gsserved || '-') - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END END AS start_rank FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON s.cdscode = t.cds WHERE s.ncesdist = '0613360' AND s.statustype = 'Active' AND CAST(s.gsserved AS TEXT) LIKE '%12' AND COALESCE(t.numtsttakr, 0) = 0) SELECT school_name, grade_span_served FROM cohort WHERE start_rank = (SELECT MIN(start_rank) FROM cohort) ORDER BY school_name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm researching the Commander banned list. Can you tell me the average mana value of the creature cards that are banned in at least one play format, considering only cards ranked in EDHRec's top 1000 most popular (ranks 1 through 1000, where rank 1 is the most popular)? Give me the average as a single number rounded to one decimal place. Keep in mind that a card printed in several sets is still just one card with one EDHRec rank and one mana value.
evidence: EDHRec rank: a card's popularity rank on EDHRec, from 1 (most popular) to 1000.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(t.cmc) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_mana_value FROM (SELECT c.name, c.convertedmanacost AS cmc FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN legalities AS l ON l.uuid = c.uuid WHERE POSITION('Creature' IN c.types) > 0 AND c.edhrecrank BETWEEN 1 AND 1000 AND l.status = 'Banned' GROUP BY c.name, c.convertedmanacost) AS t

question: For a stats segment on creature power creep, I want to size the middle-to-big power band: how many card printings have a power greater than 3 and at most 10? Note that 3 itself is out (strictly greater than 3), but 10 itself counts (at most 10). Just the total number of printings, please.
evidence: A printing is one printed appearance of a card in a set – the same card name appearing in different sets counts as several printings.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 3 AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END <= 10

question: I want a single number: how many card printings originally released in 2014 belong to a set that carries a Magic: The Gathering Online code. A set counts as MTGO-available only if its MTGO code is present for that set. By 2014 I mean the calendar year 2014 of the printing's original release date. Count each printing separately, even if the same card name appears in more than one set.
evidence: Magic: The Gathering Online (MTGO) is the official digital edition of the game; a set's MTGO code identifies that set within MTGO.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS printings FROM cards AS c JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(c.originalreleasedate AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2014' AND NOT s.mtgocode IS NULL

question: I'm putting together a report for the site owners on where people who started posting during 2010 were located, with a focus on India. Could you tell me how many of the users whose first post was created in 2010 are located in India? By 2010 I mean the calendar year 2010, and by India I mean the country itself, not any place whose name merely contains the word.
evidence: A user's first post is the earliest-created post among the posts that user owns.
gold_sql: WITH RECURSIVE fp AS (SELECT owneruserid AS uid, MIN(creaiondate) AS fdate FROM posts WHERE NOT owneruserid IS NULL GROUP BY owneruserid), locs AS (SELECT u.id AS uid, u.location AS loc FROM users AS u JOIN fp ON fp.uid = u.id WHERE fp.fdate >= '2010-01-01' AND fp.fdate < '2011-01-01'), parts(uid, head, tail) AS (SELECT uid, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN loc) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(loc AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN loc) - 1) ELSE loc END, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN loc) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(loc AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN loc) + 1) ELSE NULL END FROM locs UNION ALL SELECT uid, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN tail) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN tail) - 1) ELSE tail END, CASE WHEN POSITION(',' IN tail) > 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN tail) + 1) ELSE NULL END FROM parts WHERE NOT tail IS NULL) SELECT COUNT(*) AS users_in_india FROM parts WHERE TRIM(CAST(head AS TEXT)) = 'India'

question: I'm profiling the authors behind poorly received R posts to see if they tend to be low-reputation members. Can you give me the average reputation of the users who own posts tagged with the R tag that have a score below 20? Just the single number, rounded to the nearest whole number.
evidence: 'r' is the tag used on this site for the R programming language for statistical computing.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(u.reputation)) AS avg_reputation FROM users AS u WHERE u.id IN (SELECT p.owneruserid FROM posts AS p WHERE p.score < 20 AND CAST(p.tags AS TEXT) LIKE '%' || '<' || 'r' || '>' || '%')

question: I'd like to gauge the standing of the community members behind the R posts on one day. Could you tell me the combined reputation of the users who own the posts tagged R that were last active on 2014-08-27? I just need that one number, covering the whole calendar day 2014-08-27.
evidence: R: the R language for statistical computing.
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(reputation) AS combined_reputation FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT owneruserid FROM posts WHERE CAST(tags AS TEXT) ILIKE '%' || '<' || 'R' || '>' || '%' AND CAST(lasactivitydate AS TEXT) LIKE '2014-08-27%')

question: I'm preparing a report on international participation. How many users located in India had earned a Yearling badge before 2014? 'Before 2014' should mean before 1 January 2014. I just need the single count, nothing else.
evidence: 'Yearling' is a badge a member earns for a year of activity on the site.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.userid) AS user_count FROM badges AS t1 INNER JOIN users AS t2 ON t1.userid = t2.id WHERE CAST(t2.location AS TEXT) LIKE '%India%' AND t1.name = 'Yearling' AND t1.date < '2014-01-01'

question: I'm putting together a summary of how active badge-holders present themselves on the site. How many different display names appear among the adult users who obtained the Supporter badge? By adult I mean age 19 to 65 inclusive, and please cover all time. I just need that one number.
evidence: NaN stands for a user who never set a display name.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN u.displayname IS NULL OR u.displayname = 'NaN' THEN NULL ELSE u.displayname END) AS different_display_names FROM users AS u INNER JOIN badges AS b ON u.id = b.userid WHERE b.name = 'Supporter' AND u.age BETWEEN 19 AND 65

question: Among all posts whose title contains the phrase 'principal component scores', which one has the most related posts linked to it? For each such post, give me the post title and the number of related posts. If several posts tie for the most, list every one of them with their counts. The count should cover related posts across the site's entire history.
evidence: A related post is another post that the community's link records connect to a given post.
gold_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT p.id AS post_id, p.title AS title, COUNT(DISTINCT pl.relatedpostid) AS related_posts FROM posts AS p JOIN postlinks AS pl ON pl.postid = p.id WHERE CAST(p.title AS TEXT) LIKE '%principal component scores%' GROUP BY p.id, p.title) SELECT title, related_posts FROM counts WHERE related_posts = (SELECT MAX(related_posts) FROM counts) ORDER BY title NULLS FIRST

question: I'm trying to gauge how many users the bounty feature drew back when it first ran. How many users offered a bounty of 30 or more on some post between 1 January 2010 (inclusive) and 1 January 2011 (exclusive), going by the date the bounty was recorded? By the user who offered a bounty, I mean the post's owner - the owner account where one is recorded, otherwise the owner name on the post. I just need that one count.
evidence: A bounty is a reputation reward a user attaches to a post, recorded as an amount.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT COALESCE(CAST(p.owneruserid AS TEXT), p.ownerdisplayname)) AS users FROM votes AS v JOIN posts AS p ON v.postid = p.id WHERE v.bountyamount >= 30 AND v.creationdate >= '2010-01-01' AND v.creationdate < '2011-01-01'

question: For each month of 2010, how many posts that have no more than two answers received a link during that month? A month with none counts as zero. Give me the average across all twelve months of 2010, rounded to two decimals.
evidence: A link is a recorded connection that associates one post with another post of the site.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(month_cnt)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(month_cnt)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(12, 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average FROM (SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(t1.creationdate AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM') AS mon, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.postid) AS month_cnt FROM postlinks AS t1 INNER JOIN posts AS t2 ON t1.postid = t2.id WHERE t2.answercount <= 2 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.creationdate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2010' GROUP BY mon) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm reviewing our 2010 content. What percentage of posts created in 2010 that have a score above 5 were NOT made by high-reputation users? By high-reputation I mean a user with a reputation of at least 1000. Please give me just the single percentage value, rounded to two decimal places. Use the post's creation date to determine that it's from calendar year 2010.
evidence: high-reputation: reputation of at least 1000
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t2.reputation >= 1000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t2.reputation >= 1000 THEN 0 ELSE 1 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(t1.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM posts AS t1 LEFT JOIN users AS t2 ON t1.owneruserid = t2.id WHERE t1.score > 5 AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.creaiondate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2010'

question: I'm reviewing our 2012 performance and want to see which client segments hold our small-scale customers. For each client segment, can you tell me how many customers had total consumption below 30,000 over the whole of 2012? Please count only customers who used their cards at some point during 2012, and treat 30,000 as a strict limit - someone at exactly 30,000 doesn't count. I just need the client segment and the number of such customers per segment.
evidence: Consumption means the amount spent through a customer's fuel cards.
gold_sql: WITH yearly AS (SELECT customerid, SUM(consumption) AS total_consumption FROM yearmonth WHERE date >= '201201' AND date <= '201212' GROUP BY customerid HAVING SUM(consumption) < 30000) SELECT c.segment AS segment, COUNT(*) AS customers FROM yearly AS y INNER JOIN customers AS c ON c.customerid = y.customerid GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing 2013 uptake and want to know the genuinely active cardholder base in each client segment. For each client segment, how many of that segment's customers consumed any fuel at all during the calendar year 2013? I just need the client segment and the number of customers who consumed fuel in 2013, nothing else.
evidence: A customer's consumption for a month is the amount of fuel recorded against them for that month; by 'consumed any fuel in 2013' I mean they had fuel recorded against them in at least one month of 2013.
gold_sql: SELECT c.segment AS segment, COUNT(DISTINCT y.customerid) AS customers_with_fuel_2013 FROM customers AS c INNER JOIN yearmonth AS y ON c.customerid = y.customerid WHERE y.date BETWEEN '201301' AND '201312' AND y.consumption > 0 GROUP BY c.segment ORDER BY c.segment NULLS FIRST

question: I'm looking at a directly-funded charter high school in California with CDS code 1611190130609. Could you tell me its average SAT math score and how many students took the SAT there? Just that one school's figures. If the school with that CDS code turns out not to be directly funded, then there's no answer.
evidence: CDS code: the identification number the California Department of Education assigns to a county, district, or school. Directly-funded charter school: a charter school that receives its funding directly from the state rather than through its district.
gold_sql: SELECT t1.avgscrmath AS average_math_score, t1.numtsttakr AS number_of_test_takers FROM satscores AS t1 INNER JOIN frpm AS t2 ON t1.cds = t2.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (t1.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t1.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1611190130609 AND t2."Charter Funding Type" = 'Directly funded'

question: I want to compare how much a typical Czech-koruna-billed client spent versus a euro-billed client during 2012, to see whether the two currency segments behave differently. Please give me the difference between the average 2012 consumption of a CZK-paying customer and the average 2012 consumption of an EUR-paying customer, with the EUR average subtracted from the CZK average. Only include customers who had consumption in 2012 in each average, and the period is calendar year 2012. Just send me that one number, rounded to the nearest whole unit.
evidence: Consumption means the monthly consumption amount recorded per customer.
gold_sql: WITH per_customer AS (SELECT customerid, SUM(consumption) AS tot_2012 FROM yearmonth WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(date AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) = '2012' GROUP BY customerid) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN c.currency = 'CZK' THEN p.tot_2012 END) - AVG(CASE WHEN c.currency = 'EUR' THEN p.tot_2012 END) AS DECIMAL), 0) AS diff FROM customers AS c JOIN per_customer AS p ON c.customerid = p.customerid

question: I'm looking at SAT participation in Contra Costa County. How many schools in the county had more SAT test takers than the school with CDS code 7618040730051? That school is itself a Contra Costa County school, so I just want the count of schools strictly ahead of it by number of SAT test takers, based on the SAT results snapshot in the data. A single number is all I need.
evidence: CDS code: the County-District-School identifier that the California Department of Education assigns to each school and district in the state.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS school_count FROM satscores WHERE cname = 'Contra Costa' AND NOT sname IS NULL AND numtsttakr > (SELECT numtsttakr FROM satscores WHERE CASE WHEN (cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 7618040730051)

question: What is the average height, in centimetres, of the players taller than 180 cm who have appeared in the home team's number-3 lineup slot? This should cover the whole recorded match history with no season or date restriction. 'Taller than 180' means strictly taller than 180 cm. Please round the final average to two decimal places and return just that single value.
evidence: Number-3 lineup slot: each match records a home team's starting eleven as eleven ordered player slots; the number-3 slot is the home team's third slot.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(height) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_height FROM (SELECT p.height AS height FROM player AS p JOIN match AS m ON m.home_player_3 = p.player_api_id WHERE p.height > 180 GROUP BY p.player_api_id, p.height) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm preparing a report on team playing styles. First, consider only teams whose chance creation passing class was Risky at any point in the recorded history. Among those, I want the short names that are carried by more than one club. For each such short name, please give me: the short name, the number of clubs that carry it, and the average chance creation passing risk of those clubs that was in force on 19 September 2014, rounded to one decimal place. Sort the results by that average, highest first; if two averages are the same, order them alphabetically by short name.
evidence: A team's chance creation passing class is 'Risky' when chanceCreationPassingClass = 'Risky'; its chance creation passing risk is the chanceCreationPassing value in force on the date in question.
gold_sql: WITH risky AS (SELECT DISTINCT team_api_id FROM team_attributes WHERE chancecreationpassingclass = 'Risky'), cur AS (SELECT team_api_id, chancecreationpassing FROM team_attributes AS ta WHERE ta.date = (SELECT MAX(date) FROM team_attributes AS x WHERE x.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id AND x.date <= '2014-09-19 00:00:00')) SELECT t.team_short_name AS team_short_name, COUNT(DISTINCT t.team_api_id) AS n_teams, ROUND(CAST(AVG(c.chancecreationpassing) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS avg_passing FROM team AS t JOIN risky AS r ON r.team_api_id = t.team_api_id JOIN cur AS c ON c.team_api_id = t.team_api_id GROUP BY t.team_short_name HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT t.team_api_id) > 1 ORDER BY avg_passing DESC NULLS LAST, t.team_short_name NULLS FIRST

question: I want to gauge how tall the current medium-defensive-work players from the 1990-1995 birth cohort are. Please find the average height, in centimetres, of players born from 1990 through 1995 inclusive whose defensive work rating is medium, and round the average to two decimals. A player's rating is the grade on their most recent record that carries a grade.
evidence: The defensive work rating grades are low, medium and high.
gold_sql: WITH latest_grade AS (SELECT player_api_id, defensive_work_rate, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM player_attributes WHERE defensive_work_rate IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(p.height) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_height FROM player AS p JOIN latest_grade AS g ON g.player_api_id = p.player_api_id AND g.rn = 1 WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) BETWEEN '1990' AND '1995' AND g.defensive_work_rate = 'medium'

question: What is the average weight of all left-footed players? Round the average to one decimal place.
evidence: Left-footed means the player's preferred foot when attacking is the left one.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(weight) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_weight FROM player WHERE player_api_id IN (SELECT player_api_id FROM player_attributes WHERE preferred_foot = 'left')

question: I'm putting together a participation report for the 2015/2016 season. For every player whose name starts with Adam and who weighs more than 170, I need the number of matches he played during that season. Please return, one row per qualifying player, the player's name and his number of matches played in the 2015/2016 season, and nothing else. The season I mean is the one labeled '2015/2016'.
evidence: Played a match means being named in that match's lineup, for either the home or the away team.
gold_sql: WITH apps AS (SELECT id AS mid, home_player_1 AS pid FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_2 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_3 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_4 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_5 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_6 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_7 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_8 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_9 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_10 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, home_player_11 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_1 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_2 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_3 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_4 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_5 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_6 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_7 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_8 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_9 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_10 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016' UNION ALL SELECT id, away_player_11 FROM match WHERE season = '2015/2016') SELECT p.player_name, COUNT(a.mid) AS matches_played FROM player AS p LEFT JOIN apps AS a ON a.pid = p.player_api_id WHERE CAST(p.player_name AS TEXT) LIKE 'Adam%' AND p.weight > 170 GROUP BY p.id, p.player_name ORDER BY p.player_name COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm looking at whether a fast attacking build-up actually converts into big results. Which clubs, playing at home, have won a match by at least 3 goals while their build-up play speed was rated fast at the time? For each such club, give me the club name, short name, and how many of those home wins it has - one row per club. Please treat clubs as separate even if two clubs share the same short name, and if several clubs tie on the number of wins, list all of them. The speed rating that counts is the club's most recent rating dated on or before the match's own date.
evidence: A club wins by at least 3 goals when its goal count minus the opponent's goal count is 3 or more; 'fast' means the club's build-up play speed class at that time is Fast.
gold_sql: SELECT t.team_long_name AS club_name, t.team_short_name AS short_name, COUNT(*) AS home_wins FROM match AS m JOIN team AS t ON t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id WHERE m.home_team_goal - m.away_team_goal >= 3 AND (SELECT ta.buildupplayspeedclass FROM team_attributes AS ta WHERE ta.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id AND ta.date <= m.date ORDER BY ta.date DESC NULLS LAST, ta.id DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) = 'Fast' GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, t.team_short_name ORDER BY home_wins DESC NULLS LAST, t.team_long_name COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a report on current player abilities. How many players are over 180 cm tall and have a volley score above 70 on their most recent rating record? Judge each player by their current rating only, not their career history. For each player, use the rating record with the latest date; if a player has several rating records on that same latest date, count them only based on the single record with the highest id on that date.
evidence: By volley I mean a player's ability to strike the ball while it is in the air, and a rating record is a dated assessment of a player's attributes.
gold_sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT player_api_id, volleys, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY player_api_id ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST, id DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM player_attributes) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS tall_volley_players FROM player AS t1 INNER JOIN latest AS t2 ON t1.player_api_id = t2.player_api_id WHERE t1.height > 180 AND t2.rn = 1 AND t2.volleys > 70

question: I'm reviewing home-match outcomes by lineup slot and want one number: across the whole player population, what is the average of the total home-team goals scored in the matches where a player appeared as the home team's third listed player? In other words, for each player, take all matches where they were the home team's third listed player and add up the home team's goals in those matches; give me the average of those totals over all players, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: The home team's third listed player means the player recorded third in the home team's lineup for a match.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(m.home_team_goal) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT p.player_api_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_home_goals_per_player FROM player AS p LEFT JOIN match AS m ON m.home_player_3 = p.player_api_id

question: As of 1 January 2015, how many players preferred their left foot and had an attacking work rate below high (i.e. low or medium)? I just need the count of those players.
evidence: Attacking work rate is a rating on the scale low, medium, high; below high means low or medium. The player's preferred foot and work rate are the ones that held on 1 January 2015.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT pa.player_api_id) AS player_count FROM player_attributes AS pa JOIN (SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS latest FROM player_attributes WHERE date <= '2015-01-01 00:00:00' GROUP BY player_api_id) AS t ON pa.player_api_id = t.player_api_id AND pa.date = t.latest WHERE pa.preferred_foot = 'left' AND pa.attacking_work_rate IN ('low', 'medium')

question: What is the lowest grade level at which any school in our district begins serving students? If several schools tie at the lowest grade, just report that single grade level for the whole district. Our district is NCES district ID 0632640.
evidence: 'P' stands for preschool.
gold_sql: SELECT t1."Low Grade" AS lowest_grade FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.ncesdist = '0632640' ORDER BY (t1."Low Grade" = 'P') DESC NULLS LAST, (t1."Low Grade" = 'K') DESC NULLS LAST, CASE WHEN (t1."Low Grade") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t1."Low Grade") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END NULLS FIRST, t1."Low Grade" NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: How many players had a jumping score of 80 or higher in the player fitness assessments made between 22 February 2007 and 30 August 2007, with both of those dates included in the period? For clarity, the jumping score is the player's jumping assessment on a 1-100 scale.
evidence: jumping score: the player's jumping assessment on a 1-100 scale
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT player_api_id) AS player_count FROM player_attributes WHERE jumping >= 80 AND DATE(date) BETWEEN '2007-02-22' AND '2007-08-30'

question: What was KSV Cercle Brugge's build-up-play speed class at the time of their last match of the 2012/2013 season? The last match of the season is the latest-dated match the team played in that season, and the snapshot in effect at a moment is the latest one dated on or before that moment. I just want that single build-up-play speed class, nothing else.
evidence: Build-up-play speed class: a team's speed class for how quickly attacks are put together.
gold_sql: WITH last_match AS (SELECT MAX(m.date) AS match_day FROM match AS m JOIN team AS t ON t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id OR t.team_api_id = m.away_team_api_id WHERE t.team_long_name = 'KSV Cercle Brugge' AND m.season = '2012/2013'), effective AS (SELECT ta.buildupplayspeedclass AS speed_class FROM team_attributes AS ta JOIN team AS t2 ON t2.team_api_id = ta.team_api_id JOIN last_match AS lm ON ta.date <= lm.match_day WHERE t2.team_long_name = 'KSV Cercle Brugge' ORDER BY ta.date DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) SELECT speed_class FROM effective

question: I'm profiling how exceptional Landon Donovan was in the mid-2013 player ratings. By what percentage was his overall rating on 12 July 2013 higher than the average overall rating across all players on that same calendar date, considering every player with the overall rating they carried on that date (not only those updated that day), among players rated low, medium or high for defensive work rate? Return one value only: that percentage, rounded to two decimals (e.g. 12.34 meaning 12.34% higher).
evidence: Defensive work rate: a player's intensity of work in defense, rated low, medium or high. Overall rating: the overall score given to a player in the ratings.
gold_sql: WITH donovan AS (SELECT a.overall_rating AS r FROM player AS p JOIN player_attributes AS a ON a.player_api_id = p.player_api_id WHERE p.player_name = 'Landon Donovan' AND a.date >= '2013-07-12' AND a.date < '2013-07-13'), inforce AS (SELECT a.player_api_id AS pid, a.overall_rating AS r, a.defensive_work_rate AS dwr FROM player_attributes AS a JOIN (SELECT player_api_id, MAX(date) AS md FROM player_attributes WHERE date < '2013-07-13' GROUP BY player_api_id) AS m ON a.player_api_id = m.player_api_id AND a.date = m.md) SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * ((SELECT r FROM donovan) - AVG(r)) / NULLIF(AVG(r), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM inforce WHERE dwr IN ('low', 'medium', 'high')

question: For branch districts of accounts with loans still running in debt and recorded unemployment rates in both 1995 and 1996, list each district and the percentage change in its unemployment rate from 1995 to 1996, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Loan status 'D' denotes a running contract with the client in debt.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.a2, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (CAST(d.a13 AS DECIMAL(10, 2)) - CAST(d.a12 AS DECIMAL(10, 2))) / NULLIF(NULLIF(CAST(d.a12 AS DECIMAL(10, 2)), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM loan AS l JOIN account AS a ON l.account_id = a.account_id JOIN district AS d ON a.district_id = d.district_id WHERE l.status = 'D' AND d.a12 <> 0 AND NOT d.a13 IS NULL ORDER BY d.a2 NULLS FIRST

question: We're reviewing our first month of operations. Looking at the districts where we opened at least one account during that first month, which district had the largest population, and how many inhabitants does it have? If several districts tie for the largest population, list all of them with their populations.
evidence: The bank's first month of operation is the calendar month in which its earliest account was opened.
gold_sql: WITH first_month AS (SELECT TO_CHAR(CAST(MIN(date) AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') AS ym FROM account), first_month_districts AS (SELECT DISTINCT district_id FROM account WHERE TO_CHAR(CAST(date AS TIMESTAMP), 'YYYY-MM') = (SELECT ym FROM first_month)), cohort AS (SELECT d.a2 AS district_name, CASE WHEN (d.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((d.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS inhabitants FROM district AS d JOIN first_month_districts AS f ON d.district_id = f.district_id) SELECT district_name, inhabitants FROM cohort WHERE inhabitants = (SELECT MAX(inhabitants) FROM cohort)

question: As part of a data-quality review for a segment report, I need to know how much of the recorded transaction activity for one of our segments has no payment purpose noted. How many transactions are there, over the whole recorded history, on the accounts held by male customers born between 1974 and 1976 (birth years 1974, 1975 and 1976), for which no payment purpose is noted? Please give me just that single number.
evidence: Payment purpose: the stated reason or note recorded for a transaction.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS txn_count FROM trans AS t WHERE (t.k_symbol IS NULL OR TRIM(CAST(t.k_symbol AS TEXT)) = '') AND t.account_id IN (SELECT d.account_id FROM disp AS d INNER JOIN client AS c ON d.client_id = c.client_id WHERE c.gender = 'M' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(c.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1974' AND '1976')

question: I'm planning a card-offer mailing and want to gauge how affluent the home districts of certain clients are. Please give me one number: the average, over the districts where these clients live, of each district's average salary, rounded to two decimal places. The clients are account owners in central Bohemia who hold no credit card for their account. Two things to keep in mind: a client's district is the one recorded with the client, not the district of the account's branch; and a client counts as holding a card for an account if a card is linked to any disposition of that account, not just their own.
evidence: OWNER is the disposition type marking an account's owner; DISPONENT marks other account users.
gold_sql: WITH qualified AS (SELECT DISTINCT c.district_id FROM disp AS d JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = d.client_id JOIN district AS dist ON c.district_id = dist.district_id WHERE d.type = 'OWNER' AND dist.a3 = 'central Bohemia' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM card AS ca JOIN disp AS cd ON ca.disp_id = cd.disp_id WHERE cd.account_id = d.account_id)) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_salary FROM district WHERE district_id IN (SELECT district_id FROM qualified)

question: For the 2014-2015 academic year, what was the average number of enrolled students aged 5 to 17 eligible for free or reduced price meals per Youth Authority school? Count every Youth Authority school regardless of its status (active, closed, or merged), and treat a Youth Authority school with no meal-program record as zero. Please give me just that one number, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: A Youth Authority school is a school the state directory classifies as a Youth Authority Facility.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(COALESCE(t1."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)", 0.0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(t2.cdscode), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_frpm_ages_5_17 FROM schools AS t2 LEFT JOIN frpm AS t1 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE CAST(t2.soctype AS TEXT) LIKE '%Youth Authority%'

question: I'm preparing for a client review and want to gauge how indebted our older customers' accounts are, including accounts that never took any loans. Could you give me the average number of loans per account among accounts whose owner was born before 1950? By 'born before 1950' I mean a birth date earlier than 1 January 1950, and all loans should count regardless of when they were approved. Please give me the average rounded to two decimal places, and nothing else.
evidence: The owner of an account is the client with the OWNER disposition; a DISPONENT is a co-holder who does not own it. A loan is a credit granted on the account, recorded with the date it was approved.
gold_sql: WITH owner AS (SELECT t2.account_id, t1.birth_date FROM client AS t1 INNER JOIN disp AS t2 ON t1.client_id = t2.client_id WHERE t2.type = 'OWNER') SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(t3.loan_id)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(t3.loan_id)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT t4.account_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_loans_per_account FROM owner AS t4 LEFT JOIN loan AS t3 ON t4.account_id = t3.account_id WHERE t4.birth_date < '1950-01-01'

question: I'm putting together a periodic report on large payments made by a specific customer cohort, split by what the payment was for. Among payments over $4000 (strictly more than $4000) made from the accounts of male customers born between 1974 and 1976, I need two figures: how many were household payments, and how many were made for a purpose other than household payment. A few rules to keep in mind: born between 1974 and 1976 means the birth year is 1974, 1975 or 1976; a customer's accounts are the ones they hold a disposition on; payments are the individual transactions executed on the account, not standing payment orders; a payment counts as other-purpose only if it has a recorded purpose different from household payment, and a payment with no purpose recorded counts in neither bucket.
evidence: SIPO stands for household payment.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t.k_symbol = 'SIPO' THEN t.trans_id END) AS household_payments, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT t.k_symbol IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(t.k_symbol AS TEXT)) <> '' AND t.k_symbol <> 'SIPO' THEN t.trans_id END) AS other_purpose_payments FROM trans AS t JOIN disp AS d ON d.account_id = t.account_id JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = d.client_id WHERE c.gender = 'M' AND CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(c.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(c.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END BETWEEN 1974 AND 1976 AND t.amount > 4000

question: I want to find out whether our borrowing households from larger population centres transact differently from local ones. For every account at the Prachatice branch that has taken at least one loan, please give me: the account number, the account opening date, the total amount ever borrowed, how many outside bank counterparties the account has transacted with over its entire history, the owner's home district, the population of that district, and a rank of these borrowing households by home-district population from largest to smallest. Note that a counterparty means a particular bank account at another institution, identified by that account number, not by the bank code, and only transfers to or from another bank count — handling cash at our own branch does not involve a counterparty. A household's home district is the district its owner client is registered in, which is not necessarily Prachatice. For the ranking: largest population first, ties share the same rank and the next rank after a tie is skipped, and among households whose home districts have the same population, list the smaller account number first.
evidence: An outside bank counterparty is a bank account at another institution that money was sent to or received from on a transfer transaction. District population is the number of inhabitants of the district.
gold_sql: WITH borrowers AS (SELECT a.account_id, a.date AS opening_date, (SELECT SUM(l.amount) FROM loan AS l WHERE l.account_id = a.account_id) AS total_borrowed FROM account AS a WHERE a.district_id = (SELECT district_id FROM district WHERE a2 = 'Prachatice') AND a.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM loan)), owners AS (SELECT d.account_id, c.district_id AS home_district_id FROM disp AS d JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = d.client_id WHERE d.type = 'OWNER'), counterparties AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(DISTINCT account) AS cnt FROM trans WHERE account > 0 GROUP BY account_id) SELECT bo.account_id, bo.opening_date, bo.total_borrowed, COALESCE(cp.cnt, 0) AS counterparty_count, hd.a2 AS home_district, CASE WHEN (hd.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((hd.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS home_population, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY CASE WHEN (hd.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((hd.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END DESC NULLS LAST) AS population_rank FROM borrowers AS bo LEFT JOIN counterparties AS cp ON cp.account_id = bo.account_id LEFT JOIN owners AS o ON o.account_id = bo.account_id LEFT JOIN district AS hd ON hd.district_id = o.home_district_id ORDER BY population_rank ASC NULLS FIRST, bo.account_id ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm profiling our gold-card customers for a regional campaign, split by gender. For women first, then men, look at gold-card holders whose card's account has an average balance over 1,000. Among the branch districts holding those accounts, keep only the districts with over 100,000 inhabitants. For each gender, tell me: the number of those districts; which of them has the most inhabitants, with its inhabitants figure - if two districts tie, list both, one row per district; the average salary across those districts, rounded to two decimals; and the average ratio of urban inhabitants across those districts, rounded to two decimals. Nothing else. Please note: 'over' means strictly greater than, and an account's average balance is the mean of its balances after each transaction.
evidence: A gold card is a card of type 'gold', and its holder is the client linked to its account as type 'OWNER'. The district of an account is the district of the branch that holds it; a district's inhabitants, salary and urban-inhabitant ratio are the district's own figures.
gold_sql: WITH gold_holder AS (SELECT d.account_id, cl.gender FROM card AS c JOIN disp AS d ON c.disp_id = d.disp_id JOIN client AS cl ON d.client_id = cl.client_id WHERE c.type = 'gold' AND d.type = 'OWNER'), acct_bal AS (SELECT account_id, AVG(balance) AS avg_balance FROM trans GROUP BY account_id), holder_district AS (SELECT DISTINCT gh.gender, a.district_id FROM gold_holder AS gh JOIN account AS a ON gh.account_id = a.account_id JOIN acct_bal AS ab ON ab.account_id = a.account_id AND ab.avg_balance > 1000), big AS (SELECT hd.gender, di.a2 AS name, CASE WHEN (di.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((di.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS inhabitants, di.a11 AS salary, di.a10 AS urban FROM holder_district AS hd JOIN district AS di ON hd.district_id = di.district_id WHERE CASE WHEN (di.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((di.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END > 100000), ranked AS (SELECT gender, name, inhabitants, COUNT(*) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS district_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(salary) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_district_salary, ROUND(CAST(AVG(urban) OVER (PARTITION BY gender) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_urban_ratio, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY gender ORDER BY inhabitants DESC NULLS LAST) AS rnk FROM big) SELECT gender, district_count, name AS largest_district_name, inhabitants AS largest_district_inhabitants, avg_district_salary, avg_urban_ratio FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY CASE gender WHEN 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END NULLS FIRST, name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing a partner-bank negotiation and want to focus on our big-city clients. Please tell me, for 1998 (1 January through 31 December 1998), where the money went from gold credit card clients' accounts held at branches in large districts. Specifically: for accounts whose owner has a gold credit card, and whose branch is located in a district with at least 250,000 inhabitants, look at their outgoing payments (debit transactions, type VYDAJ). I need a ranking of the recipient bank and counter-account pairs by the total amount paid. If two pairs tie for the largest total, list both. For each pair, give me: the recipient bank code, the recipient counter-account number, the number of outgoing payments, and the total amount paid.
evidence: Gold credit card means card type 'gold'; account owner means disposition type 'OWNER'; the counter-account is the partner account at another bank to which a payment is sent; the district is the one where the account's branch is located.
gold_sql: WITH gold_accounts AS (SELECT d.account_id FROM card AS c JOIN disp AS d ON c.disp_id = d.disp_id WHERE c.type = 'gold' AND d.type = 'OWNER'), outgoing AS (SELECT t.bank AS bank, t.account AS account, COUNT(*) AS n_payments, SUM(t.amount) AS total_amount FROM trans AS t JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = t.account_id JOIN district AS di ON di.district_id = a.district_id WHERE t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM gold_accounts) AND t.type = 'VYDAJ' AND t.date >= '1998-01-01' AND t.date <= '1998-12-31' AND t.account > 0 AND CASE WHEN (di.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((di.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 250000 GROUP BY t.bank, t.account) SELECT bank, account, n_payments, total_amount FROM outgoing WHERE total_amount = (SELECT MAX(total_amount) FROM outgoing) ORDER BY bank NULLS FIRST, account NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing what the money leaving our Pisek district branch's accounts is actually used for. What percentage of the total amount of outgoing payments that state a payment purpose went to household bill payments (SIPO)? Please give me a single percentage value, rounded to two decimals. Note this should be based only on payments that state a purpose, not all outgoing payments, and should consider the full transaction history.
evidence: VYDAJ marks a transaction where money leaves the account. SIPO is the code for household bill payments. A payment states its purpose through its transaction characterization.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN t.k_symbol = 'SIPO' THEN t.amount ELSE 0 END) * 100.0 / NULLIF(SUM(t.amount), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS sipo_percentage_of_purposed_outgoing_payments FROM trans AS t JOIN account AS a ON t.account_id = a.account_id JOIN district AS d ON a.district_id = d.district_id WHERE d.a2 = 'Pisek' AND t.type = 'VYDAJ' AND NOT t.k_symbol IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(t.k_symbol AS TEXT)) <> ''

question: For planning region-targeted card offers, I need to look at the smallest markets behind each credit card type. For each credit card type (gold, classic and junior), which home district of the clients holding that type has the fewest inhabitants, and how many inhabitants does that district have? Please include all three card types, and if several districts tie for the fewest inhabitants, list them all.
evidence: By "home district" I mean the district a client lives in, and a district's inhabitants are its number of inhabitants.
gold_sql: WITH holder_districts AS (SELECT DISTINCT cd.type AS card_type, cl.district_id FROM card AS cd JOIN disp AS dp ON dp.disp_id = cd.disp_id JOIN client AS cl ON cl.client_id = dp.client_id), ranked AS (SELECT hd.card_type, ds.a2 AS district_name, CASE WHEN (ds.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((ds.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS inhabitants, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY hd.card_type ORDER BY CASE WHEN (ds.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((ds.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END NULLS FIRST) AS rnk FROM holder_districts AS hd JOIN district AS ds ON ds.district_id = hd.district_id) SELECT card_type, district_name, inhabitants FROM ranked WHERE rnk = 1 ORDER BY card_type NULLS FIRST

question:
I'm reviewing how our branches performed in 1996, and I'd like a picture of the money standing in accounts opened during that year, across the region that Litomerice belongs to (the region as given in the district table's region field).

For each district in that region where at least one account was opened in 1996 (openings counted by account creation date within the calendar year 1996), please give me:
- the district name,
- the number of accounts opened in 1996,
- the average end-of-1996 balance of those accounts,
with rows ordered by district name.

Also give me:
- the region-wide average end-of-1996 balance, taken across all those accounts (not as the mean of the district averages),
- the district with the highest average end-of-1996 balance; if two districts tie, name the one that comes first alphabetically.

By end-of-1996 balance I mean the balance after the account's last transaction dated on or before 1996-12-31; transactions dated 1997 or later don't count, and if several transactions fall on that last date, the one with the highest transaction id is the one that matters. Please round all averages to two decimals.
evidence: Balance means the balance after a transaction.
gold_sql: WITH region AS (SELECT a3 AS r FROM district WHERE a2 = 'Litomerice'), op AS (SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id FROM account AS a JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = a.district_id WHERE d.a3 = (SELECT r FROM region) AND a.date >= '1996-01-01' AND a.date < '1997-01-01'), lastd AS (SELECT t.account_id, MAX(t.date) AS md FROM trans AS t WHERE t.date <= '1996-12-31' AND t.account_id IN (SELECT account_id FROM op) GROUP BY t.account_id), lastt AS (SELECT l.account_id, MAX(t.trans_id) AS mt FROM lastd AS l JOIN trans AS t ON t.account_id = l.account_id AND t.date = l.md GROUP BY l.account_id), eb AS (SELECT x.account_id, tr.balance AS bal FROM lastt AS x JOIN trans AS tr ON tr.trans_id = x.mt), rd AS (SELECT d.a2 AS district_name, COUNT(*) AS accounts_opened_in_1996, AVG(e.bal) AS raw_avg FROM op AS o JOIN district AS d ON d.district_id = o.district_id JOIN eb AS e ON e.account_id = o.account_id GROUP BY d.district_id, d.a2) SELECT rd.district_name, rd.accounts_opened_in_1996, ROUND(CAST(rd.raw_avg AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_end_of_1996_balance, (SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(bal) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM eb) AS region_average_end_of_1996_balance, (SELECT district_name FROM rd ORDER BY raw_avg DESC NULLS LAST, district_name ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) AS district_with_highest_average_end_of_1996_balance FROM rd ORDER BY rd.district_name NULLS FIRST

question: For every district with at least 100,000 inhabitants that has withdrawal transactions, can you show me the district name, region, population, total amount withdrawn in the district, withdrawals per inhabitant (rounded to 2 decimals), the district's rank by withdrawals per inhabitant (highest first), and the average standing-order debit per account held in the district (rounded to 2 decimals)? I want to compare withdrawal pressure and the standing-order burden side by side across our major districts. Please rank all qualifying districts, not just the top few, using competition ranking so tied districts share a rank and the next rank is skipped (e.g. 1, 1, 3). The whole transaction history on record is in scope. For the average standing-order debit per account, every account held in the district counts, including ones with no standing orders – those simply bring no debits.
evidence: Withdrawal transactions are those recorded with type = 'VYDAJ'; a standing order is a recurring payment order that debits the account.
gold_sql: WITH wd AS (SELECT a.district_id, SUM(t.amount) AS total FROM trans AS t JOIN account AS a ON t.account_id = a.account_id WHERE t.type = 'VYDAJ' GROUP BY a.district_id), acct AS (SELECT district_id, COUNT(*) AS n_accounts FROM account GROUP BY district_id), so AS (SELECT a.district_id, SUM(o.amount) AS so_total FROM account AS a LEFT JOIN "order" AS o ON o.account_id = a.account_id GROUP BY a.district_id) SELECT d.a2 AS district_name, d.a3 AS region, CASE WHEN (d.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((d.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS population, wd.total AS total_withdrawn, ROUND(CAST(wd.total / NULLIF(CASE WHEN (d.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((d.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END, 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS withdrawals_per_inhabitant, RANK() OVER (ORDER BY wd.total / NULLIF(CASE WHEN (d.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((d.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END, 0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS per_inhabitant_rank, ROUND(CAST(so.so_total * 1.0 / NULLIF(acct.n_accounts, 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_standing_order_debit_per_account FROM district AS d JOIN wd ON wd.district_id = d.district_id JOIN acct ON acct.district_id = d.district_id JOIN so ON so.district_id = d.district_id WHERE CASE WHEN (d.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((d.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 100000 ORDER BY per_inhabitant_rank NULLS FIRST, district_name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm doing a lending review by account-opening year for my region. For accounts opened in the central Bohemia region from 1 January 1996 onward, broken down by the calendar year of the account creation date (as a text string like '1996', not an integer), I need: the number of accounts opened that year in the region, the total amount lent on those accounts, and the average across the districts of the amount lent per account opened in that district, rounded to two decimals. An account with no loan counts as having lent nothing.
evidence: Central Bohemia is the region value recorded for districts in the region data; the amount lent on an account is the total of the loans granted on that account.
gold_sql: WITH cba AS (SELECT a.account_id, a.district_id, EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(a.date AS TIMESTAMP)) AS y FROM account AS a INNER JOIN district AS d ON a.district_id = d.district_id WHERE d.a3 = 'central Bohemia' AND a.date >= '1996-01-01'), branch AS (SELECT cba.y, cba.district_id, SUM(COALESCE(l.amount, 0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT cba.account_id), 0) AS lent_per_account FROM cba LEFT JOIN loan AS l ON l.account_id = cba.account_id GROUP BY cba.y, cba.district_id) SELECT yt.y AS opening_year, yt.accounts_opened, yl.total_lent, ROUND(CAST(b.avg_lent AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_amount_lent_per_account FROM (SELECT y, COUNT(DISTINCT account_id) AS accounts_opened FROM cba GROUP BY y) AS yt INNER JOIN (SELECT y, SUM(l.amount) AS total_lent FROM cba LEFT JOIN loan AS l ON l.account_id = cba.account_id GROUP BY y) AS yl ON yl.y = yt.y INNER JOIN (SELECT y, AVG(lent_per_account) AS avg_lent FROM branch GROUP BY y) AS b ON b.y = yt.y ORDER BY yt.y NULLS FIRST

question: The loan of 98832 approved on January 3rd, 1996 has one applicant account. For that account, list every counterparty it had paid before January 3rd, 1996. A counterparty means a specific account number at a specific bank, so give me one row per bank code and account number combination. For each counterparty I need the bank code, the account number, the number of outgoing payments made to them, and the total amount paid to them. Count only outgoing payments (VYDAJ, i.e. debits) made before January 3rd, 1996, and sort the counterparties by total amount paid, largest first.
evidence: VYDAJ denotes an outgoing payment (debit); PRIJEM denotes an incoming payment (credit).
gold_sql: SELECT t.bank AS bank_code, t.account AS counterparty_account, COUNT(*) AS payment_count, SUM(t.amount) AS total_paid FROM trans AS t WHERE t.account_id = (SELECT l.account_id FROM loan AS l WHERE l.date = '1996-01-03' AND l.amount = 98832) AND t.type = 'VYDAJ' AND t.date < '1996-01-03' AND t.account > 0 GROUP BY t.bank, t.account ORDER BY total_paid DESC NULLS LAST

question: For the year-end review of my branch at location 1: how many accounts that were on the branch's books as of 31 December 1995 hold an active loan contract? I want a single integer, nothing else. An account counts only if it belonged to the branch on that date, and only contracts that are still active by their repayment status count - statuses A and B are finished contracts and shouldn't be included.
evidence: Loan status C means an active contract in good standing; loan status D means an active contract with the client in debt. Both are active contracts.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT a.account_id) AS account_count FROM account AS a JOIN loan AS l ON l.account_id = a.account_id WHERE a.district_id = 1 AND a.date <= '1995-12-31' AND l.status IN ('C', 'D')

question: I'm looking at the schools that the State Board of Education directly runs or charters. Which individual school among them had the most students score at least 1500 on the SAT? Please give me that school's name and its administrator's email address. If two schools tie on that count, list both.
evidence: Schools run or chartered by the State Board of Education are identified by their district ownership type.
gold_sql: SELECT t2.school, t2.admemail1 FROM satscores AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cds = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.doctype = 'State Board of Education' AND t1.rtype = 'S' AND t1.numge1500 = (SELECT MAX(t3.numge1500) FROM satscores AS t3 INNER JOIN schools AS t4 ON t3.cds = t4.cdscode WHERE t4.doctype = 'State Board of Education' AND t3.rtype = 'S')

question: I'm putting together a market-coverage report on how our 1997 rollout of monthly-statement accounts reached large urban districts. For districts with at least 100,000 inhabitants that had at least one monthly-statement account opened during calendar year 1997, please give me: the total number of monthly-statement accounts opened in those districts during 1997, how many districts are involved, and the average salary across these qualifying districts rounded to two decimals.
evidence: Monthly statement issuance means the account's statement frequency is 'POPLATEK MESICNE'.
gold_sql: WITH qualifying_districts AS (SELECT d.district_id, d.a11 FROM district AS d WHERE CASE WHEN (d.a4) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((d.a4) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 100000 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM account AS a WHERE a.district_id = d.district_id AND a.frequency = 'POPLATEK MESICNE' AND a.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31')) SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM account AS a JOIN qualifying_districts AS q ON a.district_id = q.district_id WHERE a.frequency = 'POPLATEK MESICNE' AND a.date BETWEEN '1997-01-01' AND '1997-12-31') AS monthly_accounts_opened_1997, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM qualifying_districts) AS district_count, (SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) FROM qualifying_districts) AS avg_district_salary

question: I'd like to review the breadth of each gold-card account's external payment network. For every account that has a gold credit card, could you list: the account id, the district name and region of the branch, the total amount received, the total amount withdrawn, the number of loans taken, and the number of accounts at other banks that money was transferred to or received from? Then rank the accounts by that number of external counterparties. A few things to keep in mind: if accounts tie on the number, they share a rank and the next rank is not skipped; accounts with no external counterparty transfers should still be included and count as zero; and the totals and counts should cover the full recorded period.
evidence: An external counterparty account is an account at another bank that money was transferred to or received from. Amount received refers to credit transactions, which carry transaction type PRIJEM. Amount withdrawn refers to debit transactions, which carry transaction type VYDAJ.
gold_sql: WITH gold_accounts AS (SELECT d.account_id FROM disp AS d JOIN card AS c ON c.disp_id = d.disp_id WHERE c.type = 'gold' GROUP BY d.account_id), trans_stats AS (SELECT account_id, SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'PRIJEM' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_received, SUM(CASE WHEN type = 'VYDAJ' THEN amount ELSE 0 END) AS total_withdrawn, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT bank IS NULL THEN account END) AS external_counterparty_accounts FROM trans GROUP BY account_id), loan_stats AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(loan_id) AS loan_count FROM loan GROUP BY account_id) SELECT g.account_id, di.a2 AS district, di.a3 AS region, COALESCE(t.total_received, 0) AS total_received, COALESCE(t.total_withdrawn, 0) AS total_withdrawn, COALESCE(l.loan_count, 0) AS loan_count, COALESCE(t.external_counterparty_accounts, 0) AS external_counterparty_accounts, DENSE_RANK() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(t.external_counterparty_accounts, 0) DESC NULLS LAST) AS counterparty_rank FROM gold_accounts AS g JOIN account AS a ON a.account_id = g.account_id JOIN district AS di ON di.district_id = a.district_id LEFT JOIN trans_stats AS t ON t.account_id = g.account_id LEFT JOIN loan_stats AS l ON l.account_id = g.account_id ORDER BY counterparty_rank NULLS FIRST, g.account_id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm planning services for our older female customers. For the clients who are female and were born before 1930, please look at the branches that hold their accounts, and then the districts those branches are located in. What is the average salary of those districts? Round the result to 2 decimal places. Note: born before 1930 means calendar birth dates before 1 January 1930.
evidence: Average salary refers to the district attribute describing average salary.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(d.a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_salary FROM district AS d WHERE d.district_id IN (SELECT a.district_id FROM account AS a JOIN disp AS x ON x.account_id = a.account_id JOIN client AS c ON c.client_id = x.client_id WHERE c.gender = 'F' AND c.birth_date < '1930-01-01')

question: I'm preparing a campaign for senior female clients and want a sense of the economic profile of their home districts. Could you tell me the average of the average salaries of the districts where our female clients born before 1950 live? Please give me just that single figure, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Average salary means the average yearly salary recorded for a district, in CZK.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(t1.a11) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_salary FROM district AS t1 WHERE t1.district_id IN (SELECT t2.district_id FROM client AS t2 WHERE t2.gender = 'F' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t2.birth_date AS TIMESTAMP)) < '1950')

question: I'm working on a story about campuses Los Angeles County opened during 2007 and the SAT participation they drew. What was the average number of SAT test takers per school across Los Angeles County schools that opened during 2007 and are run by a school district? Please give me that single number, rounded to two decimals. A few things to keep in mind: a county office of education counts as the school district for the schools it runs; "opened during 2007" means the opening date falls in calendar year 2007; and a school with no SAT record counts as zero test takers.
evidence: SAT test takers: the number of test takers recorded for the school.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(COALESCE(sat.numtsttakr, 0)) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_sat_test_takers FROM schools AS s LEFT JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE s.county = 'Los Angeles' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.opendate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2007' AND (CAST(s.doctype AS TEXT) ILIKE '%school district%' OR CAST(s.doctype AS TEXT) ILIKE '%county office of education%')

question: I'm comparing pit stop activity at the newer Grand Prix weekends. Among the 2017 races that were not hosted in 2000, what was the average number of pit stops per race? Please take the average of all of those races and round it to two decimal places.
evidence: Hosted in 2000 means the race was on the 2000 race calendar.
gold_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT raceid FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND NOT name IN (SELECT name FROM races WHERE year = 2000)) SELECT ROUND(CAST(1.0 * (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM pitstops WHERE raceid IN (SELECT raceid FROM cohort)) / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cohort), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_pit_stops_per_race

question: I'm writing a retrospective on German F1 drivers born between 1971 and 1985, and I'd like to quantify how often each of them reached the final part of qualifying. For every German driver born in 1971 through 1985 inclusive, over their entire career (every race on record), please give me their forename, surname, Wikipedia page link, date of birth, and the number of Q3 times they set. Sort the list from most Q3 times to fewest, and where two drivers have the same number, put the older one (by date of birth) first.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of the qualifying session that sets the starting grid; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time recorded for them in that part.
gold_sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, d.url, d.dob, COUNT(NULLIF(q.q3, '')) AS q3_times FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN qualifying AS q ON q.driverid = d.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'German' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1971' AND '1985' GROUP BY d.driverid ORDER BY q3_times DESC NULLS LAST, d.dob ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing the longest service pauses in races across the sport's whole history. Which racetrack saw the longest single pit stop ever? Please give me the racetrack name, location, country, the season year of that race, and the pit stop length. Consider all seasons in the data, and if several pit stops tie for the longest, give me one row for each of them.
evidence: pit stop: a recorded pit-stop entry in a race; pit stop length: how long that pit stop lasted
gold_sql: SELECT c.name AS racetrack, c.location, c.country, r.year AS season_year, ps.duration AS pit_stop_length FROM pitstops AS ps JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = ps.raceid JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitid = r.circuitid WHERE ps.milliseconds = (SELECT MAX(milliseconds) FROM pitstops) ORDER BY c.name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm researching the generation of drivers born in the 1980s and want to know how much final-session qualifying that generation actually did as a whole cohort. How many Q3 lap times did a driver born between 1981 and 1991 set on average? Count every driver born in that period in the average, including any who never set a Q3 lap time. Please give me the average rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session of a race weekend, whose times decide the top starting grid positions.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(COUNT(q.q3 > '' OR NULL) * 1.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT d.driverid), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_q3_times_per_driver FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN qualifying AS q ON q.driverid = d.driverid WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1981' AND '1991'

question: I'm profiling drivers whose first name alone doesn't identify them. Across all races in the dataset throughout Formula 1 history, how many qualifying 1 times slower than two minutes were set by drivers who share their first name with at least one other driver and who have no code? I want just that single count.
evidence: A driver's code is their three-letter abbreviation (e.g. 'HAM'); having no code means no such abbreviation is on record for them. The qualifying 1 time is the time a driver set in the first qualifying session of a race, one per race they took part in.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE d.code IS NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM drivers AS o WHERE o.forename = d.forename AND o.driverid <> d.driverid) AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL AND (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 2 OR (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(':' IN q.q1) - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = 2 AND CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(q.q1 AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(':' IN q.q1) + 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 0))

question: I'm checking how much of the championship points for drivers named Robert came from races covered by the lap-by-lap timing archive. For every driver whose forename is Robert, I need their reference name and the total points they scored in races where lap-by-lap timing data exists for that driver in that race. The totals should cover all seasons and races on record.
evidence: The reference name is the driver's short identifier, and points are championship points recorded for that driver's race result.
gold_sql: SELECT d.driverref AS reference_name, COALESCE(SUM(r.points), 0) AS total_points FROM drivers AS d LEFT JOIN results AS r ON r.driverid = d.driverid AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laptimes AS l WHERE l.raceid = r.raceid AND l.driverid = d.driverid) WHERE d.forename = 'Robert' GROUP BY d.driverid, d.driverref ORDER BY total_points DESC NULLS LAST, reference_name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a trivia fact about Italian drivers in Formula 1. Who holds the fastest lap time set in Q3 - the third and final part of qualifying - by an Italian driver, across the sport's entire history? Please give me the driver's forename, surname, and the fastest Q3 lap time exactly as it appears in the data. Only consider drivers who have a Q3 lap time recorded for some race, and if several Italian drivers share the exact same fastest Q3 time, list all of them.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of qualifying.
gold_sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname, q.q3 AS q3_time FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'Italian' AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying AS q2 JOIN drivers AS d2 ON d2.driverid = q2.driverid WHERE d2.nationality = 'Italian' AND q2.q3 > '')

question: I'm writing a piece on the new generation of British Formula 1 talent. Among British F1 drivers born after 1980, who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time, what was that time, and at which race and in which year was it set? Please give me the driver's full name, the race name, the race year, and the Q3 time. By 'born after 1980' I mean the year of birth is later than 1980. If two qualifying results tie for the fastest Q3 time, I'd like a row for each.
evidence: Q3 is the final part of the qualifying session that decides the front of the starting grid.
gold_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT q.driverid, q.raceid, q.q3 FROM drivers AS d JOIN qualifying AS q ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'British' AND CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(d.dob AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END > 1980 AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(q.q3 AS TEXT)) <> '') SELECT d.forename || ' ' || d.surname AS driver_name, r.name AS race_name, r.year AS race_year, c.q3 AS q3_time FROM cohort AS c JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = c.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = c.raceid WHERE c.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM cohort)

question: Who set the fastest time in Q3 (the final qualifying session) at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? Please give me the driver's reference name (the short identifier like 'hamilton') as the result. If two drivers set the same fastest Q3 time, give me both of their reference names.
evidence: Q3: the final qualifying session of a Grand Prix weekend
gold_sql: SELECT d.driverref FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE raceid = q.raceid AND NOT q3 IS NULL AND q3 <> '')

question: I'm writing a piece about how the same common forenames recur across Formula 1 history. Could you tell me how many different drivers named Peter have ever won a Formula 1 race, and the same for drivers named John? Please give me one count per forename, so I can compare the two — if they turn out to be equal, just report both counts side by side. Nothing else needed.
evidence: A race win means the driver finished first in that race.
gold_sql: SELECT t1.forename, COUNT(DISTINCT t1.driverid) AS winner_drivers FROM drivers AS t1 INNER JOIN results AS t2 ON t2.driverid = t1.driverid WHERE t2.positionorder = 1 AND t1.forename IN ('John', 'Peter') GROUP BY t1.forename ORDER BY t1.forename NULLS FIRST

question: I'm working on a story about qualifying records. Across all races, which driver set the fastest time in Q3 (the final part of qualifying)? I'd like the nationality of that driver - and if more than one driver shares the fastest Q3 time, please give me every such driver's nationality.
