I don't need anything else, just the nationality or nationalities.
evidence: Q3: the third and final part of the qualifying session.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT d.nationality FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE TRIM(CAST(q.q3 AS TEXT)) = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE NOT q3 IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(q3 AS TEXT)) <> '')

question: I'm studying how pit stop activity changed across the refuelling-rule change for Australia's F1 drivers. For each season from 2002 through 2013, can you give me the total number of pit stops made at the races of that season where, after the race, at least one Australian driver was placed better than 20th in the driver standings? I'd like the season year and the total pit stop count for each season. The pit stop total should cover every driver who pitted at those races, not just the Australian drivers.
evidence: Better than 20th in the driver standings means a position of 1 through 19 after that race. A pit stop is any recorded pit stop made by any driver at the race.
gold_sql: WITH oz_races AS (SELECT DISTINCT r.raceid, r.year FROM races AS r INNER JOIN driverstandings AS ds ON ds.raceid = r.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = ds.driverid WHERE d.nationality = 'Australian' AND ds.position <= 19 AND r.year BETWEEN 2002 AND 2013) SELECT oz.year AS season, COUNT(ps.stop) AS pit_stops FROM oz_races AS oz LEFT JOIN pitstops AS ps ON ps.raceid = oz.raceid GROUP BY oz.year ORDER BY oz.year NULLS FIRST

question: I'm profiling the oldest driver ever to win a Formula 1 race. Please identify the winning driver with the earliest date of birth - if two winning drivers share that birth date, use the one whose full name (forename then surname) comes first alphabetically. For that driver, return his full name (forename then surname), his nationality, the name and date of the first race he won (the earliest date; if two of his wins share that date, the one whose race name comes first alphabetically), and the total number of races he started over his entire career. A win means finishing in position 1 in a race. The career covers every race in the database, from 1950 through 2017. Return a single row.
evidence: Grand Prix: any race event in the database, whatever its name is; some race names do not contain the words 'Grand Prix'.
gold_sql: WITH winner AS (SELECT d.driverid, d.forename, d.surname, d.nationality FROM drivers AS d WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM results AS res WHERE res.driverid = d.driverid AND res.position = 1) ORDER BY d.dob ASC NULLS FIRST, d.forename ASC NULLS FIRST, d.surname ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) SELECT w.forename || ' ' || w.surname AS full_name, w.nationality, (SELECT r.name FROM results AS res JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = res.raceid WHERE res.driverid = w.driverid AND res.position = 1 ORDER BY r.date ASC NULLS FIRST, r.name ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) AS first_win_race, (SELECT r.date FROM results AS res JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = res.raceid WHERE res.driverid = w.driverid AND res.position = 1 ORDER BY r.date ASC NULLS FIRST, r.name ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1) AS first_win_date, (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT res.raceid) FROM results AS res WHERE res.driverid = w.driverid) AS races_started FROM winner AS w

question: I'm writing a season review piece and need the outright quickest Q2 time of the 2017 Formula One season – the fastest single Q2 time set at any race that year. Please give me the surname of the driver who set it and the name of the race where it was set. If two drivers share that fastest Q2 time, list every one of them along with the race names.
evidence: Q2: the second of the three qualifying sessions of a Grand Prix weekend.
gold_sql: WITH t AS (SELECT d.surname AS surname, r.name AS race_name, q.driverid AS driverid, q.q2 AS q2 FROM qualifying AS q JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND CAST(q.q2 AS TEXT) LIKE '%:%.%'), m AS (SELECT MIN(q2) AS q2 FROM t) SELECT t.surname, t.race_name FROM t JOIN m ON m.q2 = t.q2 ORDER BY t.driverid ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing a race report and need to name the pole-sitter by their permanent race number. Who set the fastest Q3 qualifying time at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (the race named 'Italian Grand Prix' in the 2017 season)? Please give me just that driver's permanent number. If two or more drivers share that fastest time, give me the numbers of all of them and nothing else.
evidence: Q3 is the final part of qualifying, whose times decide the top starting positions; the fastest Q3 time earns pole position.
gold_sql: SELECT d.number FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 2017 AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying AS q2 JOIN races AS r2 ON r2.raceid = q2.raceid WHERE r2.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r2.year = 2017 AND NOT q2.q3 IS NULL AND q2.q3 <> '')

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, who set the fastest lap time in Q3 (the final qualifying session), and what was that time? Give me the driver code along with the fastest Q3 time. If two or more drivers tie for the fastest Q3 time, list every tied driver.
evidence: Q3: the third and final qualifying session; a driver's Q3 time is the lap time that driver set in that session
gold_sql: SELECT t2.code, t1.q3 FROM qualifying AS t1 INNER JOIN drivers AS t2 ON t2.driverid = t1.driverid WHERE t1.raceid = (SELECT raceid FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name = 'Italian Grand Prix') AND t1.q3 <> '' AND t1.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q3) FROM qualifying WHERE raceid = (SELECT raceid FROM races WHERE year = 2017 AND name = 'Italian Grand Prix') AND q3 <> '')

question: I'm writing a report on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix (the one held in the 2017 season). Could you tell me the nationality of the driver who set the fastest time in Q3, the final part of qualifying? If several drivers share the same fastest Q3 time, please give each of their nationalities.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final part of the qualifying session.
gold_sql: SELECT d.nationality FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' AND q.q3 = (SELECT MIN(q2.q3) FROM qualifying AS q2 JOIN races AS r2 ON r2.raceid = q2.raceid WHERE r2.year = 2017 AND r2.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q2.q3 IS NULL AND q2.q3 <> '')

question: Which Chinese Grand Prix edition from the 2000s (2000–2009 seasons) had the earliest scheduled local start time? Give me the season year of that edition and the runner-up's time gap to the winner (the runner-up being the driver classified second at the finish). If several editions share the earliest scheduled local start time, use the most recent one.
evidence: Scheduled local start time: the time of day the race was scheduled to start, local to the circuit.
gold_sql: SELECT r.year, res.time AS runner_up_gap FROM races AS r JOIN results AS res ON res.raceid = r.raceid WHERE r.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND r.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 AND res.positionorder = 2 AND NOT r.time IS NULL AND r.time = (SELECT MIN(r2.time) FROM races AS r2 WHERE r2.name = 'Chinese Grand Prix' AND r2.year BETWEEN 2000 AND 2009 AND NOT r2.time IS NULL) ORDER BY r.year DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: I'm writing a qualifying report. Can you give me the driver codes of all drivers who set a time in the third qualifying session at the 2017 Italian Grand Prix? One row per driver who set such a time, and please list the codes in alphabetical order. Nothing else needed.
evidence: The third qualifying session is the final segment of the race weekend's qualifying, in which only the fastest drivers take part.
gold_sql: SELECT d.code FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND NOT q.q3 IS NULL AND q.q3 <> '' ORDER BY d.code NULLS FIRST

question: I'm writing a retrospective on the 2017 Italian Grand Prix at Monza. For the Q3 session of that race's qualifying, can you give me the permanent career race number and surname of every driver whose Q3 lap time was strictly faster than 1 minute 38.000 seconds? I want all drivers under that mark, not just the fastest, and no particular order. Note that by permanent career race number I mean the number a driver carries throughout his career, not a one-off entry number for that weekend.
evidence: Q3 is the third and final qualifying session; a driver only has a Q3 time if he actually took part in that session.
gold_sql: WITH mark(t) AS (SELECT '1' || ':' || '38.000') SELECT d.number, d.surname FROM qualifying AS q INNER JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid INNER JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.year = 2017 AND r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND CAST(q.q3 AS TEXT) LIKE '%:%' AND q.q3 < (SELECT t FROM mark) ORDER BY d.number NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying charter schools run by county offices of education. Using the K-12 school meal program records, for the charter schools these county offices operate, broken down by charter funding type (directly funded and locally funded only), I'd like to know: how many are currently operating, their total K-12 enrollment, and their total number of FRPM-eligible K-12 students. A school counts as currently operating only if its status is Active. Please give me one row per funding type, with directly funded first.
evidence: FRPM means free or reduced price meal eligibility.
gold_sql: SELECT f."Charter Funding Type" AS funding_type, COUNT(*) AS active_charter_schools, SUM(f."Enrollment (K-12)") AS total_k12_enrollment, SUM(f."FRPM Count (K-12)") AS total_frpm_students FROM frpm AS f INNER JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE f."Charter School (Y/N)" = 1 AND f."District Type" = 'County Office of Education (COE)' AND f."Charter Funding Type" IN ('Directly funded', 'Locally funded') AND s.statustype = 'Active' GROUP BY f."Charter Funding Type" ORDER BY CASE f."Charter Funding Type" WHEN 'Directly funded' THEN 1 ELSE 2 END NULLS FIRST

question: Across all seasons in the database, which circuit's Grand Prix started earliest in the day, and which started latest? I'd like the circuit reference name of the earliest one, the circuit reference name of the latest one, and the gap between those two start times in seconds. Include every season, and if several circuits share the earliest start time, list them all - same for the latest.
evidence: By "start time of the day" I mean the local clock time at the venue at which the race started.
gold_sql: WITH per_circuit AS (SELECT c.circuitref AS circuitref, MIN(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS earliest_start_seconds, MAX(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM CAST(r.time AS TIME))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS latest_start_seconds FROM races AS r JOIN circuits AS c ON c.circuitid = r.circuitid WHERE NOT r.time IS NULL GROUP BY c.circuitref) SELECT STRING_AGG(circuitref, ', ') AS earliest_circuitref, (SELECT STRING_AGG(circuitref, ', ') FROM per_circuit WHERE latest_start_seconds = (SELECT MAX(latest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit)) AS latest_circuitref, (SELECT MAX(latest_start_seconds) - MIN(earliest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit) AS gap_seconds FROM per_circuit WHERE earliest_start_seconds = (SELECT MIN(earliest_start_seconds) FROM per_circuit)

question: I'm looking into fastest race laps recorded by drivers born in the 1980s. Can you tell me which three drivers born between 1980 and 1990 reached the highest single fastest-lap speed at any point in their career? I'd like their first and last names, ranked from the highest career-high speed down, and if two drivers are tied on that speed, list the one born earlier first, and then the one whose last name comes first alphabetically. Please give me just the three names, nothing else.
evidence: Fastest lap speed: the average speed, in km/h, that a driver recorded on their single fastest lap of a race. A driver's career-high speed is based on that one lap, not an average across their laps.
gold_sql: SELECT d.forename, d.surname FROM drivers AS d JOIN results AS r ON r.driverid = d.driverid WHERE SUBSTRING(CAST(d.dob AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4) BETWEEN '1980' AND '1990' AND NOT r.fastestlapspeed IS NULL GROUP BY d.driverid, d.forename, d.surname, d.dob ORDER BY MAX(CASE WHEN (r.fastestlapspeed) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((r.fastestlapspeed) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) DESC NULLS LAST, d.dob NULLS FIRST, d.surname NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: For the 2017 Italian Grand Prix, I need the list of drivers who were eliminated after the first qualifying session. Give me one row per eliminated driver with their reference name, ordered by their first-segment time from slowest to fastest. If two eliminated drivers have the same first-segment time, list the one with the lower driverId first.
evidence: Eliminated after the first qualifying session means the driver took part in qualifying but did not go out in the second qualifying session.
gold_sql: SELECT d.driverref FROM qualifying AS q JOIN races AS r ON r.raceid = q.raceid JOIN drivers AS d ON d.driverid = q.driverid WHERE r.name = 'Italian Grand Prix' AND r.year = 2017 AND NOT q.q1 IS NULL AND (q.q2 IS NULL OR q.q2 = '') ORDER BY q.q1 DESC NULLS LAST, d.driverid NULLS FIRST

question: For the 1957 British Grand Prix, what percentage of the drivers who took part in the race were classified finishers, rounded to two decimals? By classified finisher I mean a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner. I just need the one percentage figure.
evidence: classified finisher: a driver whose race record shows them finishing the race, whether on the lead lap or one or more laps behind the winner
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT x.position IS NULL THEN x.driverid END) / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT x.driverid), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS finisher_percentage FROM races AS r JOIN results AS x ON x.raceid = r.raceid WHERE r.year = 1957 AND r.name = 'British Grand Prix'

question: I'm putting together a financial overview for the college that houses the Electrical and Computer Engineering Department. For each department of that college, can you tell me the total dues the club actually received from that department's enrolled members who took part in the club's events, in dollars? Please include every department of the college, showing zero if we received no such dues from it. Just the department name and the total dues per department.
evidence: 'Dues' is the income source label for membership dues a member pays to the club; 'Member' is the club position of an enrolled member, as opposed to officer or inactive positions.
gold_sql: SELECT m.department, COALESCE(SUM(i.amount), 0) AS total_dues_received FROM major AS m LEFT JOIN member AS mb ON mb.link_to_major = m.major_id AND mb.position = 'Member' LEFT JOIN income AS i ON i.link_to_member = mb.member_id AND i.source = 'Dues' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM attendance AS a WHERE a.link_to_member = mb.member_id) WHERE m.college IN (SELECT college FROM major WHERE department = 'Electrical and Computer Engineering Department') GROUP BY m.department ORDER BY m.department NULLS FIRST

question: For the mid-year budget review: I need to see, for each member who had to spend more than fifty dollars on an expense, how much room was still left in the budget lines those purchases were charged against. Please give me, per member, their first name, last name, and the total amount left across those budget lines in dollars rounded to two decimals. Order the results from the largest total down to the smallest; if two members have the same total, list them alphabetically by last name and then first name. The totals should cover all expenses on record, and if a budget line ended up overdrawn, its negative remaining amount should count toward the total.
evidence: Spending more than fifty dollars on an expense means the expense's dollar cost is over 50. The amount left in a budget line is the amount budgeted for that line minus the amount spent against it.
gold_sql: SELECT m.first_name, m.last_name, ROUND(CAST(SUM(b.remaining) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS remaining_total FROM member AS m JOIN (SELECT DISTINCT link_to_member, link_to_budget FROM expense WHERE cost > 50) AS e ON e.link_to_member = m.member_id JOIN budget AS b ON b.budget_id = e.link_to_budget GROUP BY m.member_id, m.first_name, m.last_name ORDER BY remaining_total DESC NULLS LAST, m.last_name ASC NULLS FIRST, m.first_name ASC NULLS FIRST

question: How many majors offered by the college that offers Tyler Hewitt's major currently have no enrolled members in the club? Count every major that college offers, by major name.
evidence: Enrolled members are the people recorded in the club's membership list.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_majors_without_members FROM major AS m WHERE m.college = (SELECT t2.college FROM member AS t1 INNER JOIN major AS t2 ON t1.link_to_major = t2.major_id WHERE t1.first_name = 'Tyler' AND t1.last_name = 'Hewitt') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM member AS mm WHERE mm.link_to_major = m.major_id)

question: For our end-of-year report, I need one figure: the average number of members who attended each event that carried a budget line for advertising, covering every such event across the club's records regardless of when it took place. Please give it as a single number rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: A budget line for advertising means a budget entry whose category is advertising.
gold_sql: WITH att AS (SELECT link_to_event, COUNT(DISTINCT link_to_member) AS members FROM attendance GROUP BY link_to_event) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(att.members, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_attendance FROM event AS t1 INNER JOIN budget AS t2 ON t2.link_to_event = t1.event_id AND t2.category = 'Advertisement' LEFT JOIN att ON att.link_to_event = t1.event_id

question: I'm a parent looking at high schools in California, and I want to know how often a school that's still open has no seniors taking the SAT at all. How many currently open public high schools in California had zero students take the SAT? By 'currently open' I mean the school's status is Active, not closed or merged. By 'high school' I mean a school whose educational instruction level is High School. Please count a school that has no SAT record at all as having zero test takers. I just want that one number.
evidence: SAT test takers: the number of test takers recorded for the school in the SAT scores data.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS zero_taker_open_high_schools FROM schools AS sc LEFT JOIN satscores AS s ON sc.cdscode = s.cds WHERE sc.statustype = 'Active' AND sc.eilname = 'High School' AND COALESCE(s.numtsttakr, 0) = 0

question: For every budget review event the club has held, can you give me the event name, its location, and the number of members who attended? I need this for the year-end report.
evidence: 'Budget' is the club's event type for its budget review events, such as the Fall Budget Review and the Spring Budget Review.
gold_sql: SELECT e.event_name, e.location, COUNT(a.link_to_member) AS attended FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON e.event_id = a.link_to_event WHERE e.type = 'Budget' GROUP BY e.event_id, e.event_name, e.location

question: I'm planning study-partner pairings around our biggest social-attendance event. Can you tell me which academic majors were most represented among the members who attended the football game? For each major, give me the major name and the number of attendees in that major. If several majors tie for the highest attendee count, list all of them, ordered alphabetically by major name.
evidence: Football game: the event named 'Football game'
gold_sql: WITH cnt AS (SELECT mj.major_name AS major_name, COUNT(DISTINCT m.member_id) AS attendees FROM event AS e JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id JOIN member AS m ON m.member_id = a.link_to_member JOIN major AS mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major WHERE e.event_name = 'Football game' GROUP BY mj.major_id, mj.major_name) SELECT major_name, attendees FROM cnt WHERE attendees = (SELECT MAX(attendees) FROM cnt) ORDER BY major_name NULLS FIRST

question: I want to gauge how much of the university's range of academic programs our club is failing to reach. Out of every major offered by the university - including majors where we have no members - what percentage have no club member studying them? Please give me just that single percentage, between 0 and 100, rounded to two decimal places.
evidence: Major: an academic program offered by the university, as listed in the club's records of majors.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN ((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM member AS mem WHERE mem.link_to_major = m.major_id))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST(((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM member AS mem WHERE mem.link_to_major = m.major_id))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM major), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage

question: For my report on the club's academic makeup, could you tell me how many members on the club roster major in a department of the College of Humanities and Social Sciences, and how many members do not? The two counts together should cover every member on the roster, with each member counted in exactly one of the two groups. A member counts as majoring in the college only if the department offering their major belongs to the College of Humanities and Social Sciences.
evidence: The College of Humanities and Social Sciences is a college made up of certain departments; membership in the college is determined by which department offers a member's major.
gold_sql: WITH flag AS (SELECT m.member_id, CASE WHEN b.college = 'College of Humanities and Social Sciences' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS in_college FROM member AS m LEFT JOIN major AS b ON m.link_to_major = b.major_id) SELECT SUM(in_college) AS members_in_college, COUNT(*) - SUM(in_college) AS members_not_in_college FROM flag

question: I'm reviewing member engagement for our club's events in MU 215. Can you give me, for each event category of events held at MU 215, the number of club members who attended those events? Please count events regardless of their status (planning, open, or closed), and make sure every category that had events at MU 215 shows up, even if none of its events had any attendees.
evidence: MU 215: the room name as the event location.
gold_sql: SELECT e.type AS event_category, COUNT(DISTINCT a.link_to_member) AS attended_members FROM event AS e LEFT JOIN attendance AS a ON a.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE e.location = 'MU 215' GROUP BY e.type

question: I'm putting together a recruitment report for the colleges and want to know which parts of the university our club's membership actually draws from. For every person on the roster-regardless of their position in the club-look at their major, and the college that houses the department offering that major. Which college or colleges do the most majors on our roster come from, and how many majors is that? If there's a tie at the top, give me every college tied at that count. Please list the colleges in alphabetical order by college name, and return just each college's name and its number of majors.
evidence: Major: a field of study offered by a department housed in a college.
gold_sql: WITH cnt AS (SELECT mj.college AS college, COUNT(DISTINCT mj.major_id) AS majors FROM member AS m JOIN major AS mj ON mj.major_id = m.link_to_major GROUP BY mj.college) SELECT college, majors FROM cnt WHERE majors = (SELECT MAX(majors) FROM cnt) ORDER BY college NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reconciling what we budgeted for September events against what we actually spent. Can you give me the total amount budgeted for the September 2019 events that served pizza? By September 2019 I mean events dated September 1 through September 30, 2019. An event counts as having served pizza if pizza was among the expenses booked to it. Please include every budget line for those events, whatever the category - not just the food lines. All I need back is the single dollar figure for that total.
evidence: A pizza expense means an expense whose description is Pizza.
gold_sql: WITH pizza_events AS (SELECT DISTINCT b.link_to_event AS event_id FROM expense AS e JOIN budget AS b ON e.link_to_budget = b.budget_id WHERE e.expense_description = 'Pizza'), sept_events AS (SELECT event_id FROM event WHERE event_date >= '2019-09-01' AND event_date < '2019-10-01') SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(b.amount) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS total_budgeted FROM budget AS b JOIN sept_events AS s ON s.event_id = b.link_to_event WHERE b.link_to_event IN (SELECT event_id FROM pizza_events)

question: I'm wrapping up the October Meeting and need the final numbers broken down by what we actually bought, not just by budget category. For every item bought with approved money for the October Meeting, can you give me: the item's name, the budget category of the purchase that included the item, and the total cost in dollars of the approved October Meeting purchases that included the item? Only expenses marked as approved count - an expense without an approval mark doesn't. If an item was included in approved purchases recorded under more than one budget category, give me one row per category. Costs should be plain sums in US dollars with no rounding, and please sort the list by category and then by item name.
evidence: An item is a single thing bought with club money, such as water, pizza or posters. A purchase is an expense recorded for the event.
gold_sql: WITH RECURSIVE split AS (SELECT link_to_budget AS bid, cost, '' AS item, expense_description || ',' AS rest FROM expense WHERE approved = 'true' UNION ALL SELECT bid, cost, TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1) FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT s.item AS item, b.category AS category, SUM(s.cost) AS total_cost FROM split AS s JOIN budget AS b ON s.bid = b.budget_id JOIN event AS e ON b.link_to_event = e.event_id WHERE s.item <> '' AND e.event_name = 'October Meeting' GROUP BY s.item, b.category ORDER BY b.category COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST, s.item COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing the year-end audit of club spending. For each item Sacha Harrison bought with club money, I need the item name and how many times she bought it. Can you give me that list?
evidence: By "item" I mean an individual thing named in a record of what money was spent for.
gold_sql: WITH RECURSIVE split(rest, item) AS (SELECT expense_description || ',', '' FROM expense WHERE link_to_member = (SELECT member_id FROM member WHERE first_name = 'Sacha' AND last_name = 'Harrison') UNION ALL SELECT SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1), TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)) FROM split WHERE rest <> '') SELECT item, COUNT(*) AS times FROM split WHERE item <> '' GROUP BY item ORDER BY item COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying the 1980 growth of public schooling in San Diego County. What was the average number of schools per month that opened in San Diego County in 1980 under a school district's jurisdiction? I need just that single number. Please average over all 12 months of 1980 (months with no openings count as zero), and give me the exact average without rounding.
evidence: A school district is a local education agency that runs K-12 public schools; it is an elementary school district, a high school district, or a unified school district.
gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (COUNT(*)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(*)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(12, 0) AS monthly_average FROM schools WHERE county = 'San Diego' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(opendate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '1980' AND doctype IN ('Elementary School District', 'High School District', 'Unified School District')

question: For our department report, I need to know how many different fields of study our club members from the Political Science Department represent. Only count members of the Political Science Department - members from other departments don't count. Just give me the number of different majors studied by those members.
evidence: A major is a field of study offered by a department.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.major_id) AS different_majors FROM member AS t1 INNER JOIN major AS t2 ON t1.link_to_major = t2.major_id WHERE t2.department = 'Political Science Department'

question: Among California schools whose students have an average SAT Math score above 400, what percentage offer virtual instruction, either exclusively or in part? Please give me a single percentage value rounded to one decimal place.
evidence: In the school directory, the exclusive-virtual category is coded 'F' and the partial-virtual category is coded 'P'.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN s.virtual IN ('F', 'P') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS pct FROM satscores AS sat JOIN schools AS s ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE sat.rtype = 'S' AND sat.avgscrmath > 400

question: I'm comparing Marvel and DC rosters and want to quantify how tall Marvel's roster is for characters whose abilities DC cannot match. What is the average height, in centimetres, of Marvel Comics characters who have at least one power that no DC Comics character has? Only characters with a measured height count.
evidence: A "power" is any single ability listed for a character in the database.
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CAST(s.height_cm AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero AS s JOIN publisher AS p ON s.publisher_id = p.id WHERE p.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND s.height_cm > 0 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM hero_power AS hp2 JOIN superhero AS s2 ON s2.id = hp2.hero_id JOIN publisher AS p2 ON p2.id = s2.publisher_id WHERE p2.publisher_name = 'DC Comics' AND hp2.power_id = hp.power_id))

question: I want to profile the cohort of heroes whose Intelligence score matches Abomination's Intelligence score. What is their average measured weight in kg? Please round the average to two decimals.
evidence: Intelligence is one of the six attribute scores a hero has (Intelligence, Strength, Speed, Durability, Power, Combat)
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN s.weight_kg > 0 THEN s.weight_kg END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN hero_attribute AS ha ON ha.hero_id = s.id JOIN attribute AS a ON a.id = ha.attribute_id WHERE a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence' AND ha.attribute_value = (SELECT abom_ha.attribute_value FROM superhero AS abom JOIN hero_attribute AS abom_ha ON abom_ha.hero_id = abom.id JOIN attribute AS abom_a ON abom_a.id = abom_ha.attribute_id WHERE abom.superhero_name = 'Abomination' AND abom_a.attribute_name = 'Intelligence')

question: I'm putting together a trivia page profiling blue-haired heroes by their abilities. For each gender, male and female, how many blue-haired superheroes have at least ten listed powers? I need the count for both groups, and by 'at least ten' I mean ten or more.
evidence: Listed powers: the superpowers recorded for a hero.
gold_sql: SELECT g.gender AS gender, COUNT(s.id) AS superhero_count FROM gender AS g LEFT JOIN superhero AS s ON s.gender_id = g.id AND s.hair_colour_id = (SELECT id FROM colour WHERE colour = 'Blue') AND (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM hero_power AS hp WHERE hp.hero_id = s.id) >= 10 WHERE g.gender IN ('Male', 'Female') GROUP BY g.gender ORDER BY g.gender NULLS FIRST

question: A parent is asking about a school and could only give me the CDS code 1612590137943. Can you look up that school and give me its name, county, district, and city; its K-12 enrollment; the number of K-12 students eligible for free or reduced price meals and the percentage eligible (report the percentage exactly as it appears, without rounding); and the SAT results - number of test takers, average reading score, average math score, average writing score, and the number of test takers whose total score is at least 1500?
evidence: CDS code: the state's County-District-School identification code assigned to each school; FRPM: the Free or Reduced Price Meal program, where the FRPM count is the number of students eligible.
gold_sql: SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.county AS county, s.district AS district, s.city AS city, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment_k12, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpm_count, f."Percent (%) Eligible FRPM (K-12)" AS pct_eligible_frpm, sat.numtsttakr AS num_sat_takers, sat.avgscrread AS avg_reading, sat.avgscrmath AS avg_math, sat.avgscrwrite AS avg_writing, sat.numge1500 AS num_ge_1500 FROM schools AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS sat ON sat.cds = s.cdscode WHERE CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1612590137943

question: For my 'giants of the genre' feature, I want to headline how varied the abilities of the tallest heroes are. How many different superpowers appear among the ten tallest superheroes? Rank heroes by height and take the top ten; if several heroes tie at the tenth-tallest height, include all of them. A hero counts among the ten tallest even if no powers are on file for them. Please give me just that single number.
evidence: superpower = an ability such as Agility or Accelerated Healing, as named in the superpower list
gold_sql: WITH top10 AS (SELECT id FROM superhero ORDER BY height_cm DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10) SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t3.power_name) AS superpowers FROM top10 JOIN hero_power AS t2 ON top10.id = t2.hero_id JOIN superpower AS t3 ON t2.power_id = t3.id

question: I'm researching heroes like A-Bomb. What is the average height in centimetres of the superheroes in A-Bomb's group? Please give me just that single number, rounded to one decimal place. Note that A-Bomb itself belongs to its group and should be included, and only heroes whose height is actually on record should count toward the average-anyone without a recorded height should be left out rather than counted as some height.
evidence: In this request, "group" refers to race.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN height_cm > 0 THEN height_cm END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_height_cm FROM superhero WHERE race_id = (SELECT race_id FROM superhero WHERE superhero_name = 'A-Bomb')

question: What is the average weight, in kg, of the heroes who belong to races in which no hero is female? Heroes whose weight is not recorded should not count toward the average. I just need that single value.
evidence: female: the hero's gender is female
gold_sql: SELECT AVG(CAST(t1.weight_kg AS DOUBLE PRECISION)) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN race AS t2 ON t1.race_id = t2.id WHERE t1.weight_kg > 0 AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM superhero AS t3 INNER JOIN gender AS t4 ON t3.gender_id = t4.id WHERE t3.race_id = t2.id AND t4.gender = 'Female')

question: For a licensing survey of non-DC heroic characters, I need a single total count of superheroes whose alignment is Good and who are not published by DC Comics. Just that one number, please.
evidence: Good means the hero's alignment is Good; DC Comics means the publisher named DC Comics.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN alignment AS t2 ON t1.alignment_id = t2.id WHERE t2.alignment = 'Good' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM publisher AS t3 WHERE t3.id = t1.publisher_id AND t3.publisher_name = 'DC Comics')

question: I'm putting together a profile of Alameda County high schools, focusing on economic disadvantage among schools that serve up through 12th grade. Among those schools, can you tell me which one has the highest free meal rate? For each school you identify, give me one line with: the school name, its free meal rate to 4 decimal places, whether it is a charter school (Yes/No/Unknown), the grades it serves, and its SAT performance level (Below Average, Average, Above Average, or No SAT Data). Please use the school's grade span of enrollment from the school directory (the GSserved field of the schools table) both to decide whether it serves up through 12th grade and for the grades-it-serves column-do not use the free-meal program record's Low Grade/High Grade for either. If several schools tie for the highest free meal rate, list every one of them.
evidence: Free meal rate = Free Meal Count (K-12) / Enrollment (K-12). SAT performance level is based on the SAT total (Reading + Math + Writing): Below Average if below 1200, Average if 1200 to 1500, Above Average if above 1500, and 'No SAT Data' if no SAT scores are available.
gold_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT f."School Name" AS school_name, f."Free Meal Count (K-12)" * 1.0 / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) AS free_rate, sc.charter, sc.gsserved, s.avgscrread, s.avgscrmath, s.avgscrwrite FROM frpm AS f LEFT JOIN schools AS sc ON sc.cdscode = f.cdscode LEFT JOIN satscores AS s ON s.cds = f.cdscode WHERE f."County Name" = 'Alameda' AND RIGHT(CAST(sc.gsserved AS TEXT), 2) = '12') SELECT school_name, ROUND(CAST(free_rate AS DECIMAL), 4) AS highest_free_meal_rate, CASE WHEN charter = 1 THEN 'Yes' WHEN charter = 0 THEN 'No' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS is_charter, gsserved AS grades_served, CASE WHEN avgscrread IS NULL THEN 'No SAT Data' WHEN avgscrread + avgscrmath + avgscrwrite < 1200 THEN 'Below Average' WHEN avgscrread + avgscrmath + avgscrwrite <= 1500 THEN 'Average' ELSE 'Above Average' END AS sat_performance FROM cohort WHERE free_rate = (SELECT MAX(f2."Free Meal Count (K-12)" * 1.0 / NULLIF(f2."Enrollment (K-12)", 0)) FROM frpm AS f2 JOIN schools AS s2 ON s2.cdscode = f2.cdscode WHERE f2."County Name" = 'Alameda' AND RIGHT(CAST(s2.gsserved AS TEXT), 2) = '12')

question: Which race is the most common among the superheroes published by the same publisher as the superhero whose full name is Charles Chandler? I'd like, for that publisher's superheroes only, the name of the most common race and the count of that publisher's superheroes of that race. Ignore any superhero with no race recorded. If several races tie for most common, list every tied race with its count.
evidence: Race: the superhero's species or type, e.g. Human, Mutant, Alien.
gold_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT r.race AS race, COUNT(*) AS hero_count FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN race AS r ON s.race_id = r.id WHERE s.publisher_id = (SELECT publisher_id FROM superhero WHERE full_name = 'Charles Chandler') AND r.race <> '-' GROUP BY r.id, r.race) SELECT race, hero_count FROM counts WHERE hero_count = (SELECT MAX(hero_count) FROM counts)

question: I'm writing a power-profile feature on heroes with super speed or death touch. Can you give me one number: the average intelligence score of the superheroes who have either of those powers? Round it to one decimal place, and only count the heroes who actually have an intelligence score in the database.
evidence: "Super speed" and "death touch" are superpower names as used in the database; "intelligence" is the hero attribute by that name.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(v) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_intelligence FROM (SELECT DISTINCT t1.id, t4.attribute_value AS v FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN hero_power AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.hero_id INNER JOIN superpower AS t3 ON t2.power_id = t3.id INNER JOIN hero_attribute AS t4 ON t4.hero_id = t1.id INNER JOIN attribute AS t5 ON t4.attribute_id = t5.id WHERE t3.power_name IN ('Super Speed', 'Death Touch') AND t5.attribute_name = 'Intelligence') AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm comparing how power-rich male and female heroes are. For all male heroes and all female heroes that have a documented real full name, what is the average number of superpowers per hero for each gender? Please compute each average over the entire hero population of that gender, not just the heroes that happen to have power records. Give me both averages, each rounded to two decimal places, and nothing else.
evidence: Full name: the hero's real, full personal name (first name plus last name, and optionally middle names); single names such as mononyms or aliases are not a full name.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Male' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_superpowers_male, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN COALESCE(pc.cnt, 0) ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN g.gender = 'Female' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_superpowers_female FROM superhero AS s INNER JOIN gender AS g ON s.gender_id = g.id LEFT JOIN (SELECT hero_id, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM hero_power GROUP BY hero_id) AS pc ON pc.hero_id = s.id WHERE CAST(s.full_name AS TEXT) LIKE '% %'

question: For the article I'm writing on heroic female characters, I'd like a physique stat for the trivia box: what is the average weight in kilograms of female superheroes whose alignment is good? Only count superheroes whose weight is known. Please round the result to two decimal places.
evidence: Alignment: the superhero's moral category, e.g. good, bad, neutral.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(s.weight_kg) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS average_weight_kg FROM superhero AS s JOIN gender AS g ON g.id = s.gender_id JOIN alignment AS a ON a.id = s.alignment_id WHERE g.gender = 'Female' AND a.alignment = 'Good' AND s.weight_kg > 0

question: I want to know about the lightest superhero whose weight has actually been recorded. Among all heroes sharing that lightest weight, give me the largest number of superpowers any of them has. If such a hero has no powers, that counts as 0. Please return just that one number.
evidence: A superpower is one power a hero has, identified by its name.
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(cnt) AS power_count FROM (SELECT COUNT(hp.power_id) AS cnt FROM superhero AS h LEFT JOIN hero_power AS hp ON h.id = hp.hero_id WHERE h.weight_kg = (SELECT MIN(weight_kg) FROM superhero WHERE weight_kg > 0) GROUP BY h.id) AS __photo_derived_1

question: I'm preparing a report on Marvel's roster and want to gauge how heroic their catalogued heroes are. Among Marvel Comics superheroes whose civilian full name is documented, what percentage are good? Please give me just that single percentage, rounded to two decimal places. Note: the percentage should be taken over all Marvel Comics superheroes with a known full name - those whose moral alignment is unknown still count toward the total, just not as good.
evidence: Good refers to alignment = 'Good'. A full name means the hero's real-world civilian identity, i.e. an actual person's name such as 'Charles Chandler' or 'Richard Milhouse Jones'.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN t3.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN t3.alignment = 'Good' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM superhero AS t1 INNER JOIN publisher AS t2 ON t1.publisher_id = t2.id LEFT JOIN alignment AS t3 ON t1.alignment_id = t3.id WHERE t2.publisher_name = 'Marvel Comics' AND NOT t1.full_name IS NULL AND t1.full_name <> '-'

question: Among distinct patients with at least one uric-acid result above the sex-specific upper limit, what is the ratio of male to female patients?
evidence: For this task, the uric-acid upper limit is 8.0 for males and 6.5 for females.
gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'M' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END / NULLIF(NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN p.sex = 'F' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 0) FROM patient AS p WHERE (p.sex = 'M' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ua > 8.0)) OR (p.sex = 'F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ua > 6.5))

question: How many distinct patients have at least one positive CRP laboratory result and no recorded patient description?
evidence: Plus-marked CRP results indicate positivity.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE CAST(l.crp AS TEXT) LIKE '%+' AND p.description IS NULL

question: How many distinct female patients have a normal anti-Scl-70 result and no recorded non-null symptom on any examination?
evidence: Normal anti-Scl-70 is recorded as 'negative' or '0'.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.sc170 IN ('negative', '0')) AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id = p.id AND NOT e.symptoms IS NULL)

question: I'm describing our young-patient group and want to show how unusual a raised RNP antibody is in these patients. Could you tell me how many patients in the thrombosis cohort born after 1 January 1960 never had a raised RNP antibody result? A few points: the group should cover every patient born after that date, including patients with no laboratory results at all - they count as never having had a raised result. "Raised" means a result strictly above 10, so a result of exactly 10 doesn't count, and a result of "negative" (no antibody detected) is never raised. Please return just one row with a single integer: the number of these patients.
evidence: RNP: anti-ribonuclear protein antibody; a result of "negative" means no antibody was detected. A raised RNP result is a laboratory result strictly above 10.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p WHERE p.birthday > '1960-01-01' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND NOT l.rnp IS NULL AND l.rnp <> 'negative' AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 10)

question: As part of the data-completeness review, I'd like to know how much laboratory follow-up our never-examined patients actually have, split by sex. Could you give me, for each sex (F and M), the average number of laboratory test dates recorded for the patients of that sex who have no examination record at all? Please cover the whole registry, all years, and round the averages to two decimal places. Nothing else needed beyond the two averages.
evidence: F denotes a female patient and M denotes a male patient. A laboratory test date is a date on which laboratory tests were recorded for a patient.
gold_sql: SELECT p.sex, ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(c.n_dates, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_lab_test_dates FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN (SELECT id, COUNT(*) AS n_dates FROM laboratory GROUP BY id) AS c ON c.id = p.id WHERE p.sex IN ('F', 'M') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM examination WHERE examination.id = p.id) GROUP BY p.sex

question: I'm reviewing autoimmune antibody profiles in our thrombosis registry. Among the female patients who were admitted to the hospital as inpatients, I need to find the laboratory test record with the highest anti-DNA antibody level, for a case review. Please give me the patient ID, the laboratory test date of that record, and the anti-DNA antibody level reported in it - nothing else. Order the results by patient ID, and if several lab test records share the highest level, list each of them.
evidence: Anti-DNA antibody level means the anti-DNA test result recorded in the laboratory tests.
gold_sql: SELECT p.id, l.date, l.dna AS anti_dna FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND p.admission = '+' AND NOT l.dna IS NULL AND CASE WHEN (l.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (l2.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l2.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM laboratory AS l2 JOIN patient AS p2 ON p2.id = l2.id WHERE p2.sex = 'F' AND p2.admission = '+' AND NOT l2.dna IS NULL) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying how concentrated economic need relates to SAT outcomes in California public schools. Among regular, non-charter schools with more than 100 K-12 students, I'd like two extremes plus one benchmark school: the school with the largest count of FRPM-eligible students, the school with the smallest FRPM share (the proportion of its K-12 enrollment that is FRPM-eligible – smallest by that share, not the raw count), and the school with CDS code 4615150435602 from my notes. If a school answers more than one part, report it once per part, and label each row with which part it answers ('largest FRPM-eligible count', 'smallest FRPM share', or 'the CDS code from my notes', in that order). Include ties. For each school, please give: school name, county, city, full mailing address as four columns (mailing street, mailing city, mailing state, mailing ZIP), website, K-12 enrollment, FRPM-eligible student count, FRPM share, average total SAT score (reading + math + writing) among its SAT takers, percentage of its SAT takers scoring 1500 or more, opening date, and status ('closed' if a closing date is recorded, otherwise 'open'). Nothing else, please.
evidence: CDS code: the California Department of Education's identification code for a school; the benchmark school in my notes is identified by CDS code 4615150435602.
gold_sql: WITH cohort AS (SELECT f.cdscode, f."School Name" AS schoolname, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" AS frpmcount, f."Enrollment (K-12)" AS enrollment, f."FRPM Count (K-12)" * 1.0 / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) AS frpmshare, CASE WHEN (f.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS code_num FROM frpm AS f WHERE f."Charter School (Y/N)" = 0 AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 100) SELECT 'largest FRPM-eligible count' AS requestpart, c.schoolname AS schoolname, s.county AS county, s.city AS city, s.mailstreet AS mailingstreet, s.mailcity AS mailingcity, s.mailstate AS mailingstate, s.mailzip AS mailingzip, s.website AS website, c.enrollment AS enrollment, c.frpmcount AS frpmcount, c.frpmshare AS frpmshare, t.avgscrread + t.avgscrmath + t.avgscrwrite AS avgtotalsat, CAST(t.numge1500 * 100.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(t.numtsttakr, 0), 0) AS pct1500plus, s.opendate AS opendate, CASE WHEN NOT s.closeddate IS NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END AS schoolstatus FROM cohort AS c JOIN schools AS s ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (t.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END WHERE c.frpmcount = (SELECT MAX(x.frpmcount) FROM cohort AS x) UNION ALL SELECT 'smallest FRPM share', c.schoolname, s.county, s.city, s.mailstreet, s.mailcity, s.mailstate, s.mailzip, s.website, c.enrollment, c.frpmcount, c.frpmshare, t.avgscrread + t.avgscrmath + t.avgscrwrite, CAST(t.numge1500 * 100.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(t.numtsttakr, 0), 0), s.opendate, CASE WHEN NOT s.closeddate IS NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END FROM cohort AS c JOIN schools AS s ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (t.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END WHERE c.frpmshare = (SELECT MIN(x.frpmshare) FROM cohort AS x) UNION ALL SELECT 'the CDS code from my notes', c.schoolname, s.county, s.city, s.mailstreet, s.mailcity, s.mailstate, s.mailzip, s.website, c.enrollment, c.frpmcount, c.frpmshare, t.avgscrread + t.avgscrmath + t.avgscrwrite, CAST(t.numge1500 * 100.0 AS DOUBLE PRECISION) / NULLIF(NULLIF(t.numtsttakr, 0), 0), s.opendate, CASE WHEN NOT s.closeddate IS NULL THEN 'closed' ELSE 'open' END FROM cohort AS c JOIN schools AS s ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (s.cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((s.cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END LEFT JOIN satscores AS t ON c.code_num = CASE WHEN (t.cds) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t.cds) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END WHERE c.code_num = 4615150435602

question: I'm writing a report section on abnormal total protein in female SLE patients and need one summary figure. Among the laboratory records of female patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus at an examination visit, where total protein is above the normal bound of 8.5, what is the average deviation of total protein from that bound across all qualifying records, rounded to three decimal places? A few points: an examination visit counts as an SLE diagnosis when systemic lupus erythematosus is among the diseases that visit's diagnosis lists, whether it's the only one or appears alongside others; the normal bound is 8.5, and a record counts as above the bound only when its TP is greater than 8.5; a record's deviation is its TP minus 8.5; and the average should cover all qualifying laboratory records across all dates.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(l.tp - 8.5) AS DECIMAL), 3) AS avg_tp_deviation FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND l.tp > 8.5 AND p.id IN (SELECT id FROM examination WHERE CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%')

question: What percentage of patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis were born in 1960 or later? Please give a single percentage rounded to one decimal place.
evidence: Psoriatic arthritis is a rheumatologic diagnosis recorded for patients in the registry.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) >= '1960' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) >= '1960' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS percentage FROM patient WHERE LOWER(TRIM(CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT))) = 'psoriatic arthritis'

question: I'm looking at patients whose anti-ribonuclear protein antibody measurement came out higher than 32. Of those patients, how many were women and how many were men? Note that 'higher than 32' means strictly above 32, not equal to it, and a patient qualifies if any of their laboratory measurements exceeded 32.
evidence: A woman means a patient recorded as F, and a man means a patient recorded as M.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.sex = 'F' THEN t1.id END) AS women, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.sex = 'M' THEN t1.id END) AS men FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 32

question: I'm studying how early in life a patient in the thrombosis cohort can show a high anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) reading. Please tell me the youngest age, in whole years, at which a patient had a laboratory test showing an anti-RNP result of at least 64. Age in whole years means the year of the test minus the year of birth. If several patients or tests share that youngest age, report that age once. I just need that single youngest age value, nothing else.
evidence: Anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody measured in the laboratory panel, reported as a titer number or as negative.
gold_sql: SELECT MIN(EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t2.date AS TIMESTAMP)) - EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS youngest_age FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 64

question: For the patients in the registry with a diagnosis of psoriatic arthritis, I'd like to know: (1) the total number of laboratory tests recorded for these patients, counting tests from all dates, and (2) how many of these patients have no laboratory tests recorded at all (i.e., patients with no laboratory record count as having no laboratory tests).
evidence: Psoriatic arthritis: a rheumatic disease diagnosis.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(l.id) AS total_tests, SUM(CASE WHEN l.id IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS no_test_patients FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE LOWER(p.diagnosis) = 'psoriatic arthritis'

question: I'm putting together a monitoring checklist for SLE patients. Among the thrombotic episodes recorded for patients diagnosed with SLE, which single symptom appears most frequently? I just need the symptom name back. Please count all recorded episodes with no date restriction. If two symptoms are equally frequent, give the one that comes first alphabetically. Note that a patient counts as having SLE only if their own diagnosis record names SLE among their diseases.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease. Thrombotic episode: an episode in which the patient experienced thrombosis.
gold_sql: WITH episodes AS (SELECT e.symptoms FROM examination AS e JOIN patient AS p ON e.id = p.id WHERE POSITION('SLE' IN p.diagnosis) > 0 AND e.thrombosis > 0) SELECT symptoms FROM episodes GROUP BY symptoms HAVING COUNT(*) = (SELECT MAX(n) FROM (SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM episodes GROUP BY symptoms) AS __photo_derived_1) ORDER BY symptoms NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: In our autoimmune disease cohort, what percentage of thrombosis patients were diagnosed with SLE at the examination visit? I need the percentage on a 0-100 scale, rounded to two decimal places. Please use the diagnosis recorded at the examination visit, not the diagnosis on the patient's overall file. This is for a write-up on which diagnoses accompany thrombotic events in this cohort.
evidence: SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus, an autoimmune disease; thrombosis: formation of a blood clot within a blood vessel
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' THEN id END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN CAST(diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' THEN id END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM examination WHERE thrombosis > 0

question: I'm reviewing thrombosis ward patients and need a chart-review list. Can you give me, for every patient who had a single lab visit where the panel showed both an LDH result strictly between 600 and 800 and urine protein of 300 mg/dL or more, the patient ID and their completed age in years as of 2026-10-09? If any one visit's panel shows both findings, that patient qualifies. Please note that a proteinuria result reported as "at least" a level counts at that stated level (e.g., "at least 300" counts as 300 mg/dL or more), and a plain number is in mg/dL. Nothing else needed, just patient ID and completed age.
evidence: Proteinuria result codes: '-' means negative, 'TR' means trace.
gold_sql: SELECT p.id, CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) < SUBSTRING(CAST(CAST(p.birthday AS CHAR(10)) AS TEXT) FROM 6 FOR 5) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END AS age FROM patient AS p WHERE NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ldh > 600 AND l.ldh < 800 AND CASE WHEN (REPLACE(REPLACE(CAST(l."U-PRO" AS TEXT), '>', ''), '=', '')) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((REPLACE(REPLACE(CAST(l."U-PRO" AS TEXT), '>', ''), '=', '')) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 300) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: In this cohort, I want to compare the most extreme total cholesterol (T-CHO) readings between patients admitted to the hospital and those followed at the outpatient clinic. Please give me, for each of the two groups, the single highest T-CHO reading, along with the admission status ('+' admitted, '-' outpatient) and the patient ID whose reading is the group's highest. List the admitted group's row first, then the outpatient group's. If several patients tie at a group's highest reading, list each of them.
evidence: T-CHO: total cholesterol. '+': the patient was admitted to the hospital. '-': the patient was followed at the outpatient clinic.
gold_sql: SELECT l."T-CHO" AS "T-CHO", p.admission AS status, p.id FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id JOIN (SELECT p2.admission AS adm, MAX(l2."T-CHO") AS mx FROM patient AS p2 JOIN laboratory AS l2 ON l2.id = p2.id WHERE p2.admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY p2.admission) AS t ON t.adm = p.admission AND t.mx = l."T-CHO" ORDER BY CASE p.admission WHEN '+' THEN 0 ELSE 1 END NULLS FIRST, p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing our cohort and need to identify patients whose most recent laboratory sample on file was collected after 1 January 1997 (strictly later than that date) and whose most recent anti-Scl-70 result on file was normal. Please return only the patient IDs for these patients.
evidence: anti-Scl-70: anti-topoisomerase I antibody, an autoantibody measured in the laboratory. A normal anti-Scl-70 result is a result of 'negative' or 0.
gold_sql: WITH lab AS (SELECT id, MAX(date) AS lastdate FROM laboratory GROUP BY id), last_sc AS (SELECT s.id AS id, s.sc170 AS sc170 FROM laboratory AS s WHERE NOT s.sc170 IS NULL AND s.date = (SELECT MAX(s2.date) FROM laboratory AS s2 WHERE s2.id = s.id AND NOT s2.sc170 IS NULL)) SELECT l.id FROM lab AS l JOIN last_sc AS c ON c.id = l.id WHERE l.lastdate > '1997-01-01' AND c.sc170 IN ('negative', '0') ORDER BY l.id NULLS FIRST

question: For a study of laboratory test patterns, I need to size a cohort. How many female patients have at least one anti-DNA antibody level below 8 (the upper bound of the normal range)? Any laboratory visit of the patient qualifies; there is no time scope. I just need that single count back.
evidence: anti-DNA level: the anti-DNA antibody concentration measured in the laboratory tests
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex = 'F' AND CASE WHEN (t2.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END < 8

question: For patients admitted to the hospital, how many never had an alkaliphosphatase level above the normal ceiling in their lab results? I just need that single count.
evidence: A patient is admitted when their status is anything other than the outpatient-clinic code; the outpatient-clinic code is '-' and admitted is '+'. A normal alkaliphosphatase level is below 300; a level of 300 or more is above the normal ceiling.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS admitted_never_high_alp FROM patient WHERE admission <> '-' AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory WHERE laboratory.id = patient.id AND alp >= 300)

question: Among patients in the thrombosis prediction database whose creatinine level is normal (below 1.5), what is the highest anti-RNP antibody level recorded? Please return just that single number; if several measurements tie for the highest, the tied value is the answer.
evidence: Anti-RNP antibody = anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, measured by the laboratory panel.
gold_sql: SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) AS max_rnp_level FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t2.cre < 1.5

question: I'm researching where high SAT performance coexists with concentrated poverty, to help target college-access support by county. For the 2014-15 academic year, for each county, how many schools had both a K-12 free-meal eligibility rate above 0.1 and at least one SAT taker scoring 1500 or higher on the school's own SAT record? Please list only counties that have at least one such school, with the county name and the number of its qualifying schools, sorted from most such schools to fewest, and alphabetically by county name when counties tie.
evidence: K-12 free-meal eligibility rate: the share of a school's K-12 enrollment that is eligible for free meals (free meal count divided by K-12 enrollment).
gold_sql: SELECT s.cname AS county, COUNT(*) AS qualifying_schools FROM satscores AS s JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = s.cds WHERE s.rtype = 'S' AND s.numge1500 > 0 AND f."Enrollment (K-12)" > 0 AND 1.0 * f."Free Meal Count (K-12)" / NULLIF(f."Enrollment (K-12)", 0) > 0.1 GROUP BY s.cname ORDER BY qualifying_schools DESC NULLS LAST, county ASC NULLS FIRST

question: In the thrombosis and autoimmune-disease cohort, I want to compare how often lactate dehydrogenase stays in the normal range between patients admitted to the hospital and patients followed at the outpatient clinic. Please give me one row per patient group showing the number of lactate dehydrogenase measurements within the normal range recorded for that group, with the admitted group's row first. Label the rows 'admitted to the hospital' for the Admission = '+' group and 'followed at the outpatient clinic' for the Admission = '-' group. Every laboratory measurement recorded for those patients across the whole study period counts. Nothing else is needed.
evidence: The normal range for lactate dehydrogenase means a value below 500.
gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN p.admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS patient_group, COUNT(*) AS normal_ldh_measurements FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') AND l.ldh < 500 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY patient_group

question: For patients whose sex is not recorded in the registry, I need two counts for the annual quality report: how many have at least one laboratory result on file, and of those, how many have at least one laboratory result showing elevated total bilirubin. The report covers all dates.
evidence: A patient's sex is not recorded when the registry holds no sex entry for that patient. Total bilirubin of 2.0 or higher counts as elevated.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.id) AS patients_with_lab_results, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t2."T-BIL" >= 2.0 THEN t2.id END) AS patients_with_elevated_bilirubin FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex IS NULL OR t1.sex = ''

question: For an audit, I need the number of admitted female patients born between 1945 and 1989 (inclusive) who have an ANA examination where the observed pattern is exactly P, with no other pattern alongside it. Please return just that single count.
evidence: ANA pattern: the pattern observed in the ANA examination, e.g. 'P' or 'P,S'; the admission mark starting with a plus indicates the patient was admitted.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN examination AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE CAST(t1.admission AS TEXT) LIKE '+%' AND t1.sex = 'F' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(t1.birthday AS TIMESTAMP)) BETWEEN '1945' AND '1989' AND t2."ANA Pattern" = 'P'

question: Among the patients in the thrombosis prediction data, how many have a first laboratory record showing both a normal glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (GOT) level and an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) concentration? By normal GOT I mean a value below 60, and by elevated RNP I mean a value above 10. By first laboratory record I mean the one with the earliest laboratory test date for that patient. I need just a single count of these patients.
evidence: GOT stands for glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase (also known as aspartate aminotransferase, AST); RNP stands for anti-ribonuclear protein.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT l.id) FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.date = (SELECT MIN(date) FROM laboratory WHERE id = l.id) AND l.got < 60 AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 10

question: I'm reviewing the current kidney involvement status of the thrombosis prediction cohort. For every patient who has had a proteinuria test, I need their patient identifier, sex, the date of their most recent proteinuria test, and the proteinuria level measured on that test. "Most recent" means the latest proteinuria test by test date.
evidence: A proteinuria test is a test that measures the level of protein in the urine; the proteinuria level is the result value it reports.
gold_sql: SELECT p.id AS patient_id, p.sex AS sex, l.date AS most_recent_test_date, l."U-PRO" AS proteinuria_level FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE NOT l."U-PRO" IS NULL AND l.date = (SELECT MAX(l2.date) FROM laboratory AS l2 WHERE l2.id = l.id AND NOT l2."U-PRO" IS NULL) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing patients with an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein result. Among patients who ever had an anti-ribonuclear protein result of 16 or higher, I want to follow up the three whose liver enzymes stayed in the normal range. The normal range for GPT is below 60. For each patient, take their highest GPT value among their laboratory tests that fall in the normal range. Rank patients from that highest value down; if two patients share the same value, the one with the smaller patient ID comes first. Please return exactly three patients, one row per patient, with only each patient's Birthday.
evidence: GPT stands for glutamic pyruvic transaminase, a liver enzyme; anti-ribonuclear protein is an autoantibody measured in laboratory tests.
gold_sql: SELECT t1.birthday FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t2.gpt < 60 AND t1.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE CASE WHEN (rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 16) GROUP BY t1.id ORDER BY MAX(t2.gpt) DESC NULLS LAST, t1.id ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: I'm trying to size a subgroup in the thrombosis cohort: how many female patients had a normal prothrombin time (below 14 seconds) along with an elevated anti-ribonuclear protein level (16 or higher)? Please use the prothrombin time and anti-ribonuclear protein level from the same laboratory record for each patient. I just need the count of such female patients.
evidence: Normal prothrombin time: below 14 seconds. Elevated anti-ribonuclear protein: a measured level of 16 or higher.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS t1 INNER JOIN laboratory AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex = 'F' AND t2.pt < 14 AND CASE WHEN (t2.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((t2.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 16

question: I have a school on file with CDS code 1611430131177. Find the school in the same county as that school whose own SAT record shows the most students scoring at least 1500 (not a district-wide roll-up). If two schools tie on that count, use the one with the smaller CDS code. Send me that school's administrator's first and last name.
evidence: CDS code: the County-District-School identifier assigned to each school; scoring at least 1500: a test taker whose combined SAT score is 1500 or higher.
gold_sql: SELECT s.admfname1, s.admlname1 FROM satscores AS x JOIN schools AS s ON s.cdscode = x.cds JOIN frpm AS f ON f.cdscode = x.cds WHERE x.rtype = 'S' AND s.county = (SELECT county FROM schools WHERE CASE WHEN (cdscode) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((cdscode) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = 1611430131177) ORDER BY x.numge1500 DESC NULLS LAST, CASE WHEN (f."School Code") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((f."School Code") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I need to find lupus patients with liver lab abnormalities. Can you give me the ID and sex of every patient who has at least one total bilirubin (T-BIL) result at or above the upper normal limit of 1.2 mg/dL, and who has a confirmed diagnosis of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)? SLE counts if it's among the patient's confirmed diagnoses, even when other diseases are diagnosed or suspected alongside it, but a suspected SLE alone doesn't count. The diagnosis should be the patient's overall diagnosis, not something noted at a single examination. Please order results by sex, then patient ID, and return only the ID and sex.
evidence: T-BIL: total bilirubin; SLE: systemic lupus erythematosus; susp.: suspected, not a confirmed diagnosis
gold_sql: SELECT p.id, p.sex FROM patient AS p WHERE p.id IN (SELECT id FROM laboratory WHERE "T-BIL" >= 1.2) AND POSITION(',' || 'SLE' || ',' IN ',' || REPLACE(p.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') > 0 ORDER BY p.sex NULLS FIRST, p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing how often older female patients show elevated anti-RNP antibody results, split by whether they were admitted to the hospital or followed at the outpatient clinic. For female patients aged at least 50 as of 2026-10-09, please give me a two-row breakdown by care setting (admitted to the hospital vs. followed at the outpatient clinic), showing for each setting how many patients had at least one anti-RNP laboratory result of at least 4, and how many had no such result. A patient's admission marker of '+' counts as admitted to the hospital and '-' counts as followed at the outpatient clinic; patients with any other admission marker are out of scope. Order the two rows alphabetically by care setting.
evidence: anti-RNP: anti-ribonuclear protein antibody, measured in laboratory results; admission marker: the patient's recorded admission sign.
gold_sql: SELECT CASE WHEN p.admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 4) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS patients_with_rnp_at_least_4, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 4) THEN 0 ELSE 1 END) AS patients_without_such_result FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND p.birthday <= CAST((CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - 50) || SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 5) AS DATE) AND p.admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY care_setting NULLS FIRST

question: Among all patients diagnosed with systemic lupus erythematosus, I want to find the patient whose anti-DNA test result was the strongest ever recorded for that disease. Please report the patient's identifier, the patient's diagnosis, and that patient's highest anti-DNA test result, using the number exactly as the test wrote it. If several patients tie for the highest anti-DNA result, list every tied patient.
evidence: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is an autoimmune disease; anti-DNA is an antibody test reported as a number.
gold_sql: WITH ranked AS (SELECT p.id AS patient_id, p.diagnosis AS diagnosis, l.dna AS highest_anti_dna, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY p.id ORDER BY CASE WHEN (l.dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END DESC NULLS LAST, l.date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM patient AS p INNER JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE CAST(p.diagnosis AS TEXT) LIKE '%SLE%' AND NOT l.dna IS NULL), best AS (SELECT patient_id, diagnosis, highest_anti_dna FROM ranked WHERE rn = 1) SELECT patient_id, diagnosis, highest_anti_dna FROM best WHERE CASE WHEN (highest_anti_dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((highest_anti_dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (highest_anti_dna) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((highest_anti_dna) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END) FROM best) ORDER BY patient_id NULLS FIRST

question: For our thrombosis study cohort, I'd like to know how often patients have a normal IgG status at their most recent check, broken down by care setting.
