Please give me, for patients admitted to the hospital and for patients followed at the outpatient clinic, the percentage of that setting's patients whose most recent IgG measurement was normal. The percentage should be out of every patient in that setting, so patients who never had an IgG measurement count toward the denominator but not the numerator. Please round to one decimal place, and label the two results exactly as 'admitted to the hospital' and 'followed at the outpatient clinic'.
evidence: An IgG measurement is considered normal when it is above 900 and below 2000.
gold_sql: WITH latest AS (SELECT id, igg, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY id ORDER BY date DESC NULLS LAST) AS rn FROM laboratory WHERE NOT igg IS NULL) SELECT CASE WHEN p.admission = '+' THEN 'admitted to the hospital' ELSE 'followed at the outpatient clinic' END AS care_setting, ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN l.igg > 900 AND l.igg < 2000 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(COUNT(p.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS patient_share FROM patient AS p LEFT JOIN latest AS l ON l.id = p.id AND l.rn = 1 WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1 NULLS FIRST

question: I'm putting together a renal-involvement review. Could you pull the demographics of patients who show both marked tissue damage and clinically significant proteinuria? Specifically, I need the patient ID, sex, and birthday of every patient who has at least one LDH result of 500 or higher and at least one urinary protein result of 100 mg/dL or more. A few details: an LDH of exactly 500 counts, and a urinary protein of exactly 100 mg/dL counts. The qualifying LDH and the qualifying urinary protein don't have to come from the same lab visit. Please give me one row per patient, ordered by patient ID, and nothing beyond those three fields.
evidence: Urinary protein is reported in mg/dL; a dipstick grade may carry the equivalent concentration in mg/dL in parentheses, e.g. '+2(100)' is 100 mg/dL. A result written as '>=' followed by a value means at least that many mg/dL, e.g. '>=300' is 300 mg/dL or more. 'TR' means a trace and '-' means none detected; any other marker is not a quantified mg/dL concentration. An LDH of 500 or higher is outside the normal range.
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT p.id, p.sex, p.birthday FROM patient AS p WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.ldh >= 500) AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS u WHERE u.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) LIKE '%(%' THEN CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") + 1 FOR POSITION(')' IN u."U-PRO") - POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") - 1)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") + 1 FOR POSITION(')' IN u."U-PRO") - POSITION('(' IN u."U-PRO") - 1)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END WHEN CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) LIKE '>=%' THEN CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM 3)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(u."U-PRO" AS TEXT) FROM 3)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END ELSE CASE WHEN (u."U-PRO") IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((u."U-PRO") AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END END >= 100) ORDER BY p.id NULLS FIRST

question: I'm reviewing confirmed SLE cases for a study of neurologic involvement. Among patients whose examination lists SLE among the diagnosed diseases and who have a symptom recorded at such an examination, I need the case detail of the youngest such patient. Please send me the symptom recorded at that qualifying examination and that patient's overall diagnosis (their overall diagnosis, not the diagnosis written at the examination). If two patients share the same birth date, use the one with the smaller patient ID; and if that patient has more than one qualifying examination, use the most recent one.
evidence: SLE is systemic lupus erythematosus. A disease name followed by 'susp' means the disease was only suspected, not diagnosed.
gold_sql: WITH target AS (SELECT 'SLE' AS d) SELECT e.symptoms, p.diagnosis AS overall_diagnosis FROM patient AS p JOIN examination AS e ON e.id = p.id WHERE NOT p.birthday IS NULL AND NOT e.symptoms IS NULL AND TRIM(CAST(e.symptoms AS TEXT)) <> '' AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM target WHERE REPLACE(',' || REPLACE(e.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',', ',' || d || ',', '') <> ',' || REPLACE(e.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') ORDER BY p.birthday DESC NULLS LAST, p.id NULLS FIRST, e."Examination Date" DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: I'm auditing inpatient intake during the February 1998 admission wave. Among patients first seen at the hospital in the second half of February 1998 (visit date from 15 to 28 February 1998), find the oldest inpatient at first presentation and give me that patient's diagnosis only. If two patients tie in age, use the one with the smaller patient ID.
evidence: 'Inpatient' means the patient was admitted to the hospital rather than followed at the outpatient clinic, regardless of whether the record notes extra detail about the admission.
gold_sql: SELECT p.diagnosis FROM patient AS p WHERE p."First Date" >= '1998-02-15' AND p."First Date" <= '1998-02-28' AND CAST(p.admission AS TEXT) LIKE '+%' ORDER BY p.birthday ASC NULLS FIRST, p.id ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: I need to size a comparison group for my study of liver-enzyme abnormalities. How many patients in the registry have never had an ALT result above the normal range? Please give me the count broken down by sex: the number of male patients and the number of female patients. Every patient in the registry counts, including patients with no laboratory results at all, since they have never had an abnormal result. The report should cover exactly the two sexes, male and female.
evidence: ALT is measured by the GPT laboratory value; a GPT result of 60 or higher exceeds the normal range.
gold_sql: SELECT p.sex AS sex, COUNT(*) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p WHERE p.sex IN ('M', 'F') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.gpt >= 60) GROUP BY p.sex ORDER BY p.sex NULLS FIRST

question: For patients with at least one red-blood-cell result below 3.5 (RBC), I need a breakdown by care setting: how many patients were admitted to the hospital (+) versus followed at the outpatient clinic (-), and the average completed age of each group on 2026-10-09, rounded to one decimal place. Age means completed years on 2026-10-09.
evidence: Red-blood-cell result below 3.5 (RBC); admission status + marks a patient admitted to the hospital, - marks a patient followed at the outpatient clinic.
gold_sql: SELECT p.admission AS care_setting, COUNT(*) AS patient_count, ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST('2026-10-09' AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST('2026-10-09' AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN TO_CHAR(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM-DD') < TO_CHAR(CAST(p.birthday AS TIMESTAMP), 'MM-DD') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_age FROM patient AS p WHERE p.admission IN ('+', '-') AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND l.rbc < 3.5) GROUP BY p.admission ORDER BY p.admission COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST

question: I'm studying antiphospholipid antibodies in Sjögren's syndrome (SJS). Could you tell me the average anti-cardiolipin IgM concentration among SJS patients, rounded to two decimal places? To clarify: use only patients with an established SJS diagnosis recorded at the patient level (a diagnosis marked 'susp', such as 'SJS susp', is only a suspicion and those patients should not be included). Include every examination recorded for these patients regardless of date. A recorded anti-cardiolipin IgM value of 0 means the antibody was not detected at that examination, so treat it as no measurement and leave it out of the average - count only examinations where a concentration was detected.
evidence: SJS is the abbreviation used for Sjögren's syndrome; a diagnosis marked 'susp' (e.g. 'SJS susp') is only a suspicion of the disease, not an established diagnosis.
gold_sql: WITH RECURSIVE tokens AS (SELECT id, '' AS tok, COALESCE(diagnosis, '') || ',' AS rest FROM patient UNION ALL SELECT id, TRIM(CAST(SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR POSITION(',' IN rest) - 1) AS TEXT)), SUBSTRING(CAST(rest AS TEXT) FROM POSITION(',' IN rest) + 1) FROM tokens WHERE rest <> '') SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN e."aCL IgM" > 0 THEN e."aCL IgM" END) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS avg_acl_igm FROM examination AS e WHERE e.id IN (SELECT id FROM tokens WHERE tok = 'SJS')

question: I'm planning reviews of Provision 2 meal programs under the NSLP and want to see which cities concentrate magnet schools under that provision. For each city that has at least one, can you give me the number of the city's magnet schools that run a Provision 2 meal program? Use the city where the school is located, not its mailing city. Also, if a school's NSLP entry lists multiple provision types, don't count it as running Provision 2.
evidence: NSLP is the National School Lunch Program. Provision 2 is a federal provision under the NSLP that lets a school serve meals at no charge to all students regardless of family income.
gold_sql: SELECT s.city AS city, COUNT(*) AS magnet_schools FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE s.magnet = 1 AND CAST(f."NSLP Provision Status" AS TEXT) LIKE '%Provision 2%' GROUP BY s.city ORDER BY magnet_schools DESC NULLS LAST, city NULLS FIRST

question: How many female patients have a Sjögren's syndrome diagnosis recorded in a medical examination? Please count across the full examination history with no date restriction, and note that suspected cases don't count—only an actual SjS diagnosis should be included. I just need that single number.
evidence: SjS is the standard medical abbreviation for Sjögren's syndrome, and the diagnosis is recorded under that abbreviation.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) AS n_female_sjs_patients FROM patient AS t1 JOIN examination AS t2 ON t1.id = t2.id WHERE t1.sex = 'F' AND CAST((',' || REPLACE(t2.diagnosis, ' ', '') || ',') AS TEXT) LIKE ('%' || ',' || 'SjS' || ',' || '%')

question: How many patients who were never admitted to the hospital (outpatient follow-up only) had at least one normal anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) result? A normal RNP result means the test found no anti-ribonuclear protein antibody: a negative result, or a measured value of zero. I just need a single number.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP): an antibody test
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS patient_count FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON p.id = l.id WHERE p.admission = '-' AND l.rnp IN ('negative', '0')

question: In our autoimmune-cohort registry, I'm profiling young patients with strongly positive anti-RNP findings. What is the average age, in years, of the patients who were younger than 70 as of 2026-10-09 and who have at least one anti-RNP result of 64 or higher? Please give the average as a single number to one decimal place.
evidence: anti-ribonuclear protein (anti-RNP) result: the reading recorded for a patient's anti-RNP test in the laboratory record
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 6) < SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DECIMAL), 1) AS average_age FROM patient AS p WHERE (CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 1 FOR 4)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN SUBSTRING(CAST('2026-10-09' AS TEXT) FROM 6) < SUBSTRING(CAST(p.birthday AS TEXT) FROM 6) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) < 70 AND EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM laboratory AS l WHERE l.id = p.id AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END >= 64)

question: I'd like a single number: how many female patients in the thrombosis prediction data have a laboratory record showing a normal white blood cell count, an abnormal fibrinogen level, and an anti-ribonuclear protein (RNP) reading above 15, considering all recorded laboratory dates?
evidence: A normal white blood cell count means strictly between 3.5 and 9.0; an abnormal fibrinogen level means at most 150 or at least 450.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) FROM patient AS p JOIN laboratory AS l ON l.id = p.id WHERE p.sex = 'F' AND l.wbc > 3.5 AND l.wbc < 9.0 AND (l.fg <= 150 OR l.fg >= 450) AND CASE WHEN (l.rnp) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((l.rnp) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > 15

question: Among molecules containing at least one single bond, what is the average number of oxygen atoms per molecule? Include molecules with no oxygen and round to four decimal places.
evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.
gold_sql: WITH molecules AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '-'), oxygen AS (SELECT molecule_id, COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom WHERE element = 'o' GROUP BY molecule_id) SELECT ROUND(CAST(AVG(COALESCE(oxygen.n, 0)) AS DECIMAL), 4) FROM molecules LEFT JOIN oxygen ON oxygen.molecule_id = molecules.molecule_id

question: I'm preparing a mailing campaign and need a list of public high schools in Los Angeles County that have more than 500 free or reduced-price meal recipients ages 5-17. By public high schools I mean every public high-school category in the meal program report - regular high schools, continuation high schools, and high schools in single-school districts - not just regular ones; middle and junior high schools don't count. For each school, please give me the school name exactly as listed in the school directory, plus the campus (physical) street address - not a mailing or post-office address - along with the city, state and ZIP code, each as a separate field. Schools sharing a name are separate schools, so one row per school. Please sort the list by school name.
evidence: 'Free or reduced-price meal recipients ages 5-17' refers to the count reported in the meal program report for students ages 5-17 receiving free or reduced-price meals.
gold_sql: SELECT s.school AS school_name, s.street, s.city, s.state, s.zip FROM frpm AS f JOIN schools AS s ON f.cdscode = s.cdscode WHERE f."County Name" = 'Los Angeles' AND CAST(f."School Type" AS TEXT) LIKE '%High School%' AND CAST(f."School Type" AS TEXT) NOT LIKE '%Junior%' AND f."FRPM Count (Ages 5-17)" > 500 ORDER BY s.school COLLATE "C" NULLS FIRST, s.cdscode NULLS FIRST

question: Which elements have the fewest atom occurrences across non-carcinogenic molecules? Include all elements tied for the minimum.
evidence: A '-' carcinogenicity label means non-carcinogenic.
gold_sql: WITH counts AS (SELECT a.element, COUNT(*) AS n FROM atom AS a JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = a.molecule_id WHERE m.label = '-' GROUP BY a.element) SELECT element FROM counts WHERE n = (SELECT MIN(n) FROM counts) ORDER BY element NULLS FIRST

question: How many distinct iodine atoms and distinct sulfur atoms, respectively, participate in at least one single bond?
evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.element = 'i' THEN t1.atom_id ELSE NULL END) AS iodine_nums, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN t1.element = 's' THEN t1.atom_id ELSE NULL END) AS sulfur_nums FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN connected AS t2 ON t1.atom_id = t2.atom_id INNER JOIN bond AS t3 ON t2.bond_id = t3.bond_id WHERE t3.bond_type = '-'

question: What is the most common bond type in molecule TR010, and is that molecule carcinogenic? Return the bond type and YES or NO.
evidence: In this dataset, a molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '-' is not.
gold_sql: SELECT b.bond_type, CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 'YES' ELSE 'NO' END FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR010' GROUP BY b.bond_type, m.label ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC NULLS LAST, b.bond_type NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1

question: Among all atoms in molecules containing at least one single bond, what percentage are chlorine atoms? Round to four decimal places.
evidence: The '-' bond-type symbol denotes a single bond.
gold_sql: WITH molecules AS (SELECT DISTINCT molecule_id FROM bond WHERE bond_type = '-') SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN a.element = 'cl' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) / NULLIF(NULLIF(COUNT(*), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 4) FROM molecules AS m JOIN atom AS a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id

question: I want to know whether molecular saturation is associated with carcinogenicity in our compound library. Please report, for molecules in which every bond is a single bond: the number of carcinogenic molecules minus the number of non-carcinogenic molecules. And for all other molecules: the same difference (carcinogenic count minus non-carcinogenic count). Rules: label '+' means the molecule is carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic; bond type '-' denotes a single bond; each molecule belongs to exactly one of the two groups.
evidence: In the labels, '+' indicates a carcinogenic molecule and '-' indicates a non-carcinogenic molecule; for bond types, '-' indicates a single bond.
gold_sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule AS m WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_molecules_with_only_single_bonds, (SELECT SUM(CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN 1 ELSE -1 END) FROM molecule AS m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-')) AS diff_other_molecules

question: In our toxicology library, how many carbon-carbon pairs joined by a double bond are there in total across the carcinogenic compounds? I want a single number for the whole library.
evidence: A compound is carcinogenic when its label is '+' and non-carcinogenic when its label is '-'. In the bond notation, '-' is a single bond, '=' is a double bond, and '#' is a triple bond.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS num_pairs FROM connected AS c JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE m.label = '+' AND b.bond_type = '=' AND a1.element = 'c' AND a2.element = 'c' AND c.atom_id < c.atom_id2

question: For the carcinogenic molecules in the toxicology database, how many carbon-carbon bonds are there of each bond type (single, double, and triple)? Please give me the bond type and the corresponding count.
evidence: A molecule labelled '+' is carcinogenic. Bond types are recorded as follows: a single bond as '-', a double bond as '=', and a triple bond as '#'. A carbon-carbon bond is a bond whose two bonded atoms are both carbon.
gold_sql: SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = b.molecule_id WHERE a1.element = 'c' AND a2.element = 'c' AND m.label = '+' GROUP BY b.bond_type ORDER BY b.bond_type NULLS FIRST

question: I want to know how widely chlorine atoms bond to other atoms across the toxicology database. Please give me a single number: the count of atoms that bond with chlorine atoms. Nothing else.
evidence: Chlorine means the element recorded under the code cl.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a1.element = 'cl' THEN c.atom_id2 ELSE c.atom_id END) AS bonded_atoms FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a1 ON c.atom_id = a1.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id WHERE a1.element = 'cl' OR a2.element = 'cl'

question: I'm studying the immediate chemical environment of sulfur atoms in carcinogenic molecules. Please tell me, as a single number, how many atoms are directly bonded to a sulfur atom in carcinogenic molecules. A molecule labeled '+' is carcinogenic; a molecule labeled '-' is not.
evidence: Sulfur refers to the element 's'. A direct bond is a bond between two atoms.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t2.atom_id2) AS atom_count FROM atom AS t1 INNER JOIN connected AS t2 ON t1.atom_id = t2.atom_id INNER JOIN molecule AS m ON t1.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE t1.element = 's' AND m.label = '+'

question: I'm building a control group of nitrogen-containing structures for a carcinogenicity review. How many molecules in the database contain at least one nitrogen atom, where none of those nitrogen atoms takes part in a double bond or a triple bond? A nitrogen held only by single bonds is fine; any nitrogen in a double or triple bond disqualifies the molecule. Molecules with no nitrogen at all don't count. I just need the single number of such molecules.
evidence: Nitrogen refers to the element code 'n'; '=' denotes a double bond; '#' denotes a triple bond; '-' denotes a single bond.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS number_of_molecules FROM molecule AS m WHERE EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'n') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM atom AS a2 INNER JOIN connected AS c ON c.atom_id = a2.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a2.atom_id INNER JOIN bond AS b ON b.bond_id = c.bond_id WHERE a2.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a2.element = 'n' AND b.bond_type <> '-')

question: For a report on structural features of carcinogenic compounds, I'm looking at compounds that form a triple bond. Among those, what percent are labeled carcinogenic and what percent are labeled non-carcinogenic, each rounded to two decimal places? The two percents should sum to 100, apart from rounding.
evidence: Label '+' means carcinogenic; label '-' means non-carcinogenic.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN b.molecule_id END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '+' THEN b.molecule_id END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT b.molecule_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct_carcinogenic, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '-' THEN b.molecule_id END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN m.label = '-' THEN b.molecule_id END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(DISTINCT b.molecule_id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct_non_carcinogenic FROM bond AS b JOIN molecule AS m ON b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id WHERE b.bond_type = '#'

question: I'm characterizing how strongly rare chemical elements are integrated into the molecular skeleton of carcinogenic compounds. For every carcinogenic molecule that contains at least one atom of an element that appears in no other molecule in the database, I want the number of bonds its atoms of that element take part in. Please judge an element's rarity over every molecule in the database, carcinogenic or not. Return the molecule_id and that bond count for each qualifying molecule, one row per molecule, sorted by molecule_id.
evidence: '+' is the label of a carcinogenic molecule, '-' of a non-carcinogenic one; a bond is a link between two atoms of a molecule.
gold_sql: WITH rare AS (SELECT element FROM atom GROUP BY element HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT molecule_id) = 1) SELECT m.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS bond_count FROM molecule AS m INNER JOIN atom AS a ON a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id LEFT JOIN connected AS c ON (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) WHERE m.label = '+' AND a.element IN (SELECT element FROM rare) GROUP BY m.molecule_id ORDER BY m.molecule_id NULLS FIRST

question: I'd like a ranked inventory of every molecule in the toxicology database that contains at least one carbon atom. For each qualifying molecule, give me its molecule id, carcinogenicity label, number of atoms, number of bonds, number of carbon atoms, number of chlorine atoms, number of carbon-touching bonds, and number of multiple bonds - one row per molecule, including molecules where some of these counts are zero. Rank the rows from the most carbon-touching bonds to the fewest; break ties by larger total atom count, then by molecule id ascending. Give consecutive rank positions 1, 2, 3, ... with no gaps after ties.
evidence: A carbon-touching bond is a bond with a carbon atom at one of its ends; a bond between two carbon atoms counts as one bond. A multiple bond is a double or triple bond. The carcinogenicity label '+' means carcinogenic, '-' means not carcinogenic.
gold_sql: WITH carbonbonds AS (SELECT a.molecule_id, COUNT(DISTINCT c.bond_id) AS carbon_bond_count FROM connected AS c JOIN atom AS a ON c.atom_id = a.atom_id WHERE a.element = 'c' GROUP BY a.molecule_id), moleculestats AS (SELECT m.molecule_id, m.label, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id) AS atom_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id) AS bond_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'c') AS carbon_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM atom AS a WHERE a.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND a.element = 'cl') AS chlorine_count, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bond AS b WHERE b.molecule_id = m.molecule_id AND b.bond_type <> '-') AS multiple_bond_count FROM molecule AS m WHERE m.molecule_id IN (SELECT molecule_id FROM atom WHERE element = 'c')), ranked AS (SELECT ms.molecule_id, ms.label, ms.atom_count, ms.bond_count, ms.carbon_count, ms.chlorine_count, COALESCE(cb.carbon_bond_count, 0) AS carbon_touching_bonds, ms.multiple_bond_count, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY COALESCE(cb.carbon_bond_count, 0) DESC NULLS LAST, ms.atom_count DESC NULLS LAST, ms.molecule_id NULLS FIRST) AS position FROM moleculestats AS ms LEFT JOIN carbonbonds AS cb ON cb.molecule_id = ms.molecule_id) SELECT position, molecule_id, label, atom_count, bond_count, carbon_count, chlorine_count, carbon_touching_bonds, multiple_bond_count FROM ranked ORDER BY position NULLS FIRST

question: For molecule TR377, I'd like a profile of its bond composition, covering single and double bonds only. For each bond kind, please give me: the bond kind symbol, the number of bonds of that kind in the molecule, and the number of element pairs that bond kind joins. Also include the molecule's carcinogenicity label. List the bond kinds from most frequent to least; if two kinds are equally frequent, list them alphabetically by symbol.
evidence: A single bond is shown as the symbol '-' and a double bond as '='; a molecule label '+' means carcinogenic and '-' means not carcinogenic.
gold_sql: WITH scoped AS (SELECT bond_type, COUNT(*) AS bond_count FROM bond WHERE molecule_id = 'TR377' AND bond_type IN ('-', '=') GROUP BY bond_type), pairs AS (SELECT b.bond_type, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN a1.element < a2.element THEN a1.element || '-' || a2.element ELSE a2.element || '-' || a1.element END) AS pair_count FROM bond AS b JOIN connected AS c ON c.bond_id = b.bond_id JOIN atom AS a1 ON a1.atom_id = c.atom_id JOIN atom AS a2 ON a2.atom_id = c.atom_id2 WHERE b.molecule_id = 'TR377' AND b.bond_type IN ('-', '=') GROUP BY b.bond_type) SELECT s.bond_type, s.bond_count, p.pair_count, m.label AS molecule_label FROM scoped AS s JOIN pairs AS p ON p.bond_type = s.bond_type JOIN molecule AS m ON m.molecule_id = 'TR377' ORDER BY s.bond_count DESC NULLS LAST, s.bond_type NULLS FIRST

question: I'm screening for molecules to flag for follow-up. Can you give me the molecule_id of the first three molecules, in alphabetical order, that are non-carcinogenic, contain at least one metal atom, and have single bonds between their atoms? Please return only the molecule ids.
evidence: A molecule label of '-' means the molecule is non-carcinogenic. A bond type of '-' means a single bond between two atoms. The metals are sodium (na), potassium (k), calcium (ca), copper (cu), zinc (zn), tin (sn), lead (pb), magnesium (mg) and lithium (li).
gold_sql: SELECT DISTINCT t1.molecule_id FROM molecule AS t1 INNER JOIN bond AS t2 ON t1.molecule_id = t2.molecule_id INNER JOIN atom AS t3 ON t1.molecule_id = t3.molecule_id WHERE t2.bond_type = '-' AND t1.label = '-' AND t3.element IN ('na', 'k', 'ca', 'cu', 'zn', 'sn', 'pb', 'mg', 'li') ORDER BY t1.molecule_id NULLS FIRST LIMIT 3

question: For molecule TR397, I want to see which elements form the bonding skeleton. For each element present among its atoms, how many atoms of that element take part in at least one bond? Please report two things per row: the element symbol (e.g. c, h, o) and the number of that element's atoms in TR397 that take part in a bond. One row per element, ordered alphabetically by element symbol. Only atoms belonging to TR397 should count.
evidence: Takes part in a bond: the atom is one of the two atoms a bond joins.
gold_sql: SELECT a.element, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN NOT c.bond_id IS NULL THEN a.atom_id END) AS bonded_atoms FROM atom AS a LEFT JOIN connected AS c ON (c.atom_id = a.atom_id OR c.atom_id2 = a.atom_id) WHERE a.molecule_id = 'TR397' GROUP BY a.element ORDER BY a.element NULLS FIRST

question: How many distinct card printings with no recorded power value or a variable power expression have at least one ruling mentioning 'triggered ability'?
evidence: An asterisk anywhere in a power expression denotes variable power.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT t1.id) FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN rulings AS t2 ON t1.uuid = t2.uuid WHERE (t1.power IS NULL OR CAST(t1.power AS TEXT) LIKE '%*%') AND CAST(t2.text AS TEXT) LIKE '%triggered ability%'

question: Among card printings with no recorded power value or a variable power expression, what percentage have a French translation? Round to two decimals.
evidence: An asterisk anywhere in a power expression denotes variable power.
gold_sql: SELECT ROUND(CAST(100.0 * (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT c.uuid) FROM cards AS c JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE (c.power IS NULL OR CAST(c.power AS TEXT) LIKE '%*%') AND f.language = 'French') / NULLIF(NULLIF((SELECT COUNT(*) FROM cards WHERE power IS NULL OR CAST(power AS TEXT) LIKE '%*%'), 0), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2)

question: How many black-border cards with power 10 or greater are available on Magic: The Gathering Online? I just want a single number.
evidence: Black-border cards are the tournament-legal Magic cards, excluding the joke silver-bordered sets. Power is the first number in the lower-right corner of a creature card.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(id) FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'black' AND CAST(availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%mtgo%' AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 10

question: I have the count of sets with fewer than five translations of their name — now I need the gap in cards to size the translation budget. Can you give me the total number of cards contained in those sets? A few things to keep in mind: 'fewer than five' is strict, so a set with exactly five translations doesn't count. All sets count regardless of type or release (core set, expansion, promotional, online-only, etc.). If two languages have the identical translated name string for a set, that's one translation, not two. And a set's card count should be its full size, including promotional and related supplemental printings.
evidence: A 'translation of a set's name' means the localized name of the set in another language, e.g. its French or Simplified Chinese name.
gold_sql: SELECT SUM(totalsetsize) AS total_cards FROM sets WHERE (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT translation) FROM set_translations WHERE setcode = sets.code) < 5

question: I'm preparing a multilingual catalog and want to gauge how much localizable content exists per kind of set. For every set type, I need the number of sets of that type that have an officially translated name, and the total number of cards in those sets. Please include every set type in the results, even ones where no set has an officially translated name (show zero for both values in that case), and sort the results alphabetically by set type.
evidence: Set type: the expansion type of a set, such as core, expansion or promo. Officially translated name: the set's name rendered in another language, such as Italian or Chinese Traditional.
gold_sql: SELECT s.type, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code) THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS sets_with_translation, SUM(CASE WHEN EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM set_translations AS t WHERE t.setcode = s.code) THEN s.totalsetsize ELSE 0 END) AS total_cards FROM sets AS s GROUP BY s.type ORDER BY s.type NULLS FIRST

question: What is the Percent (%) Eligible Free (K-12) in the school administered by an administrator whose first name is Alusine. List the district code of the school.
evidence: K-12 free-meal eligibility percentage is K-12 free-meal recipients divided by K-12 enrollment, times 100.
gold_sql: SELECT t1."Free Meal Count (K-12)" * 100 / NULLIF(t1."Enrollment (K-12)", 0), t1."District Code" FROM frpm AS t1 INNER JOIN schools AS t2 ON t1.cdscode = t2.cdscode WHERE t2.admfname1 = 'Alusine'

question: I'm tracking printings of Tarmogoyf. Of all its printings, which frame version is the newest? Please give me the year that identifies that latest frame version, and the percentage of the card's printings that use it, rounded to two decimal places. The percentage should be over all printings of the card.
evidence: A printing is an occurrence of the card in a set; a frame version is the version of the card frame style of a printing.
gold_sql: WITH target AS (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) AS yr FROM cards WHERE name = 'Tarmogoyf') SELECT t.yr AS frame_version_year, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = t.yr THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = t.yr THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100 / NULLIF(COUNT(c.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS percentage FROM cards AS c CROSS JOIN target AS t WHERE c.name = 'Tarmogoyf' GROUP BY t.yr

question: I'm brewing and looking for cards that combine two keyword abilities. How many cards in the collection have both Flying and Cycling? Note that each printing counts as its own card, and a card only counts if it has both keywords.
evidence: Flying and Cycling are keyword abilities in Magic: The Gathering.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cards WHERE POSITION(',' || 'Flying' || ',' IN ',' || keywords || ',') > 0 AND POSITION(',' || 'Cycling' || ',' IN ',' || keywords || ',') > 0

question: I'm comparing how mana-cheap Magic: The Gathering sets have become over time. For two sets — the set where Abyssal Horror was first printed, and the most recently released set in the database — I want one row per set with the set name and the percentage of that set's cards that have a mana cost whose converted mana cost is 3 or less, rounded to two decimal places. By "first printed", I mean the set with the earliest release date among the sets Abyssal Horror appears in; if several share that earliest date, use the one whose set code comes first alphabetically. For the most recent set, use the latest release date among all sets; if several share that date, again take the one whose set code comes first alphabetically. By "converted mana cost" I mean the card's mana value, and a card counts as having a mana cost only if a mana cost is printed on it.
evidence: Converted mana cost means the card's mana value; a card has a mana cost when a mana cost is printed on the card.
gold_sql: WITH first_set AS (SELECT s.code, s.name, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s WHERE s.code IN (SELECT c.setcode FROM cards AS c WHERE c.name = 'Abyssal Horror') ORDER BY s.releasedate ASC NULLS FIRST, s.code ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1), latest_set AS (SELECT s.code, s.name, s.releasedate FROM sets AS s ORDER BY s.releasedate DESC NULLS LAST, s.code ASC NULLS FIRST LIMIT 1), chosen AS (SELECT code, name, releasedate FROM first_set UNION ALL SELECT code, name, releasedate FROM latest_set) SELECT ch.name AS set_name, ROUND(CAST(CASE WHEN (SUM(CASE WHEN NOT c.manacost IS NULL AND c.manacost <> '' AND c.convertedmanacost <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((SUM(CASE WHEN NOT c.manacost IS NULL AND c.manacost <> '' AND c.convertedmanacost <= 3 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END * 100.0 / NULLIF(COUNT(c.id), 0) AS DECIMAL), 2) AS pct FROM chosen AS ch JOIN cards AS c ON c.setcode = ch.code GROUP BY ch.code, ch.name, ch.releasedate ORDER BY ch.releasedate ASC NULLS FIRST

question: How many different cards have ever been printed as a release promotion? I just need a single number, covering all printings across the game's entire history with no time restriction. Note that a prerelease printing is a different promotion type and shouldn't be counted as a release promotion.
evidence: A release promotion is a promotional printing whose promotion type is 'release'.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT name) AS release_promo_cards FROM cards WHERE CAST(REPLACE(promotypes, 'prerelease', '') AS TEXT) LIKE '%release%'

question: I'm cataloguing the Abzan clan's cards and need this: among the cards with the Abzan watermark, which one comes last in its set's numbering - i.e. has the highest collector number? Please give me the card's name, its collector number, and how many foreign-language printings exist for that card. If several Abzan-watermarked cards tie for the highest collector number, list every one of them, each with its own count of foreign-language printings. Count each foreign-language edition record of the card as one printing.
evidence: Abzan watermark: the clan mark printed on the card. Collector number: the number of the card within the set it was printed in. Foreign-language printing: the foreign-language edition record of a card.
gold_sql: SELECT c.name AS card_name, c.number AS collector_number, COUNT(f.id) AS foreign_printings FROM cards AS c LEFT JOIN foreign_data AS f ON f.uuid = c.uuid WHERE c.watermark = 'abzan' AND CASE WHEN (c.number) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.number) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = (SELECT MAX(CASE WHEN (number) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((number) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END) FROM cards WHERE watermark = 'abzan') GROUP BY c.uuid, c.name, c.number ORDER BY c.name NULLS FIRST

question: I'm profiling the weak end of the white-bordered printings. How many white-bordered cards have a power less than 3? I just need that single count - only white-bordered cards are in scope, and please don't include anything else in the answer.
evidence: Power is a card's combat strength. A card whose power is shown as * has no known power.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS weak_attackers FROM cards WHERE bordercolor = 'white' AND NOT power IS NULL AND power <> '*' AND power = CAST(CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AS TEXT) AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END < 3

question: I'm putting together a showcase of instant-speed cards from Magic: The Gathering. Which cards in the Dark Ascension set have the Flash keyword and, among those, the highest converted mana cost? Please list just the card names, one row per card, alphabetically by name, and include every card that ties on that highest cost.
evidence: Dark Ascension is the Magic: The Gathering set named 'Dark Ascension'. Flash is the keyword that lets a card be cast any time you could cast an instant. Converted mana cost is the total amount of mana a card costs to cast.
gold_sql: SELECT t1.name FROM cards AS t1 INNER JOIN sets AS t2 ON t2.code = t1.setcode WHERE t2.name = 'Dark Ascension' AND POSITION(',' || 'Flash' || ',' IN ',' || t1.keywords || ',') > 0 AND t1.convertedmanacost = (SELECT MAX(t3.convertedmanacost) FROM cards AS t3 INNER JOIN sets AS t4 ON t4.code = t3.setcode WHERE t4.name = 'Dark Ascension' AND POSITION(',' || 'Flash' || ',' IN ',' || t3.keywords || ',') > 0) ORDER BY t1.name ASC NULLS FIRST

question: I'm preparing localized set icon assets and need to know the foreign-language name coverage of every Magic: The Gathering set released in 2020. For each set released in 2020 (meaning its release date falls within the calendar year 2020), please give me the set's name, its keyrune code, and the number of languages in which the set has an official translated name. Nothing else.
evidence: keyrune code: the code for the set's image icon; official translated name: the set's name rendered in a foreign language by the game's publisher.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name, s.keyrunecode, COUNT(DISTINCT st.language) AS translated_languages FROM sets AS s LEFT JOIN set_translations AS st ON st.setcode = s.code AND NOT st.translation IS NULL WHERE EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.releasedate AS TIMESTAMP)) = '2020' GROUP BY s.id, s.name, s.keyrunecode ORDER BY s.name NULLS FIRST

question: I collect trading cards, and one of my favorites is Ancestor's Chosen. Of all the sets that include this card, look at the one released most recently - if several sets share that latest release date, consider them together. How many creature cards in that set (or sets) have power greater than toughness? I just want that single count, nothing else.
evidence: Power is the attack strength printed on a creature card; toughness is the defense strength printed on a creature card.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS power_over_toughness FROM cards WHERE CAST(types AS TEXT) LIKE '%Creature%' AND CASE WHEN (power) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((power) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END > CASE WHEN (toughness) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((toughness) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?([0-9]+([.][0-9]*)?|[.][0-9]+)([eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?'), '0') AS DOUBLE PRECISION) END AND setcode IN (SELECT c2.setcode FROM cards AS c2 JOIN sets AS s2 ON s2.code = c2.setcode WHERE c2.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen' AND s2.releasedate = (SELECT MAX(s3.releasedate) FROM sets AS s3 JOIN cards AS c3 ON c3.setcode = s3.code WHERE c3.name = 'Ancestor''s Chosen'))

question: Among the Commander-leadable cards that the Card Kingdom catalog lists for both a foil printing and a regular non-foil printing – cards listed for only one of the two printings don't count – I want the single most recent card frame year (the latest calendar year among the frame versions), and the count of cards in that group whose frame version is that year. Please return just that one row: the frame year and its card count.
evidence: A card 'may lead a Commander deck' if it can be the deck's commander – the one card that leads the deck and sets its color identity – not merely be included among the deck's other cards.
gold_sql: WITH cmd AS (SELECT frameversion, SUBSTRING(CAST(leadershipskills AS TEXT) FROM POSITION('commander' IN leadershipskills)) AS tail FROM cards WHERE NOT cardkingdomid IS NULL AND NOT cardkingdomfoilid IS NULL) SELECT frameversion AS frame_year, COUNT(*) AS card_count FROM cmd WHERE CASE WHEN (LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) >= 0 THEN SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM LENGTH(CAST('commander' AS TEXT)) + LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT)) FOR LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) ELSE SUBSTRING(CAST(tail AS TEXT) FROM GREATEST(1, (LENGTH(CAST('commander' AS TEXT)) + LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) + (LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT)))) FOR LEAST(-(LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))), (LENGTH(CAST('commander' AS TEXT)) + LENGTH(CAST('True' AS TEXT))) - 1)) END = 'True' GROUP BY frameversion ORDER BY CASE WHEN (frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

question: Which card whose original type is 'Creature - Elf' has received the most rulings, and how many rulings has it received? I want the card name and the number of rulings. A card and all of its printings/reprints count as one and the same card. If several cards tie for the most rulings, list every one of them.
evidence: A ruling is an official rules clarification issued for a card, on the date it was issued.
gold_sql: WITH elf_cards AS (SELECT DISTINCT name FROM cards WHERE originaltype = 'Creature - Elf'), elf_rulings AS (SELECT c.name, r.date, r.text FROM cards AS c JOIN rulings AS r ON c.uuid = r.uuid WHERE c.name IN (SELECT name FROM elf_cards) GROUP BY c.name, r.date, r.text), counts AS (SELECT name, COUNT(*) AS ruling_count FROM elf_rulings GROUP BY name) SELECT name, ruling_count FROM counts WHERE ruling_count = (SELECT MAX(ruling_count) FROM counts) ORDER BY name NULLS FIRST

question: I play paper Magic and I'm building a pauper deck. How many printings of cards illustrated by Erica Yang are legal in the pauper format and exist as paper (physically printed) cards? I want just a single count of printings, with each printing counted separately.
evidence: Pauper is a Magic: The Gathering format where only common-rarity cards are legal; a printing is a specific physical or digital release of a card in a set; 'legal in pauper' means the card's pauper legality status is Legal; 'paper' means a physical printed card.
gold_sql: SELECT COUNT(*) AS paper_pauper_printings FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN legalities AS l ON c.uuid = l.uuid WHERE c.artist = 'Erica Yang' AND l.format = 'pauper' AND l.status = 'Legal' AND CAST(c.availability AS TEXT) LIKE '%paper%'

question: I'm researching printings of the Magic: The Gathering card Tarmogoyf. I want to identify every reprint of Tarmogoyf that was published in a card frame style that was already at least 10 full years old when the set came out. Please give me the set name and release date of every set that qualifies, not just one. Two rules: the frame version is the year that frame style dates from (the frame style itself, not any frame artwork effects), and 'at least 10 full years' is inclusive, measured between the frame version's year and the set's release year.
evidence: Frame version: the year the card frame style of a printing dates from.
gold_sql: SELECT s.name AS set_name, s.releasedate AS release_date FROM cards AS c INNER JOIN sets AS s ON s.code = c.setcode WHERE c.name = 'Tarmogoyf' AND c.frameversion ~ '^[0-9]+$' AND CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END = CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END AND CASE WHEN (EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.releasedate AS TIMESTAMP))) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((EXTRACT(YEAR FROM CAST(s.releasedate AS TIMESTAMP))) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END - CASE WHEN (c.frameversion) IS NULL THEN NULL ELSE CAST(COALESCE(SUBSTRING(CAST((c.frameversion) AS TEXT) FROM '^[[:space:]]*[+-]?[0-9]+'), '0') AS BIGINT) END >= 10
